Moscow has withdrawn its UK ambassador as relations between Britain and Russia continue to deteriorate amid Vladimir Putin’s war on Ukraine.

Former Russian ambassador to the UK Andrey Kelin left his post on July 21, having been in the role for over seven years.

According to The Times, Russia is yet to submit another candidate to the Foreign Office and there is reportedly no indication of when a replacement may be appointed.

The Russian embassy in London denied Russia intends to downgrade diplomatic relations between Moscow and Britain, but said ties have “deteriorated to an unprecedentedly low level entirely on London's initiative”.

A spokesman for the Russian embassy told The Times that the former ambassador had made “considerable efforts to preserve contacts and channels of communication” with the UK but accused the government of choosing a “path of confrontation” with Russia.

open image in gallery It is unclear why Mr Kelin left his post after his seven-year tenure ( PA Archive )

“He left Britain in the hope that a more constructive and respectful dialogue could eventually be restored, should the UK reconsider its policies towards our country,” the spokesman said.

“In the meantime, the embassy is headed by the chargé d’affaires.”

A FCDO spokesperson said: “This is a matter for the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

“We have an Ambassador and Embassy in Moscow to engage and raise concerns with the Russian government.

“We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine, which has the right to defend itself against Russia’s illegal and unprovoked invasion.”

It comes as relations between the Kremlin and Downing Street continue to suffer, amid Putin’s ongoing war on Ukraine.

Last week, Russia’s embassy to the UK said reports that Ukrainian forces had used unmanned aircraft manufactured by two UK companies “confirm that London is deliberately opting for an escalation of the Ukraine crisis”.

open image in gallery It comes as relations between the Kremlin and Downing Street continue to suffer, amid Putin’s ongoing war on Ukraine. ( AFP/Getty )

It accused Britain of “seeking to contain Russia and inflict maximum damage on it by proxy” and warned that the deeper its involvement becomes, “the higher the price it will pay”.

“London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which it will have to answer,” it said.

But prime minister Andy Burnham hit back, saying Britain would not be deterred by the threats.

Asked what his message to Putin was after Russia accused the UK of escalating the war, Mr Burnham said: “This is the UK doing what it has long said it would do, which is to support Ukraine 100 per cent against this illegal war led by Vladimir Putin.

“We are providing support so that Ukraine can defend itself, and that’s been the British position all the way through this conflict by previous prime ministers.

“It remains the case with me. We are not fair weather friends. We will be there in Ukraine’s hour of need, and that won’t change.”

It is unclear why Mr Kelin left his post after his seven-year tenure.

Last year, he denied Russian involvement in the 2018 Salisbury poisonings, claiming they were ‘staged’ in an plot reminiscent of an Agatha Christie novel.

News.title: Norris wins incident-packed Dutch Grand Prix as Russell loses ground again
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris passed Kimi Antonelli and Lewis Hamilton in the space of a single lap before holding on to win the Dutch Grand Prix for back-to-back Formula One victories.

Norris started on pole but was overtaken by Antonelli at a restart after the race was stopped for a heavy crash by hometown driver Max Verstappen, who was unhurt, during the second lap.

Norris reeled in Antonelli before passing him around the outside of the first corner in a daring move on lap 54 of 72, then took the lead from Ferrari’s Hamilton before the lap was over.

The defending champion held on with old tyres to take the win. “This fight is still on,” he said over team radio.

“The move [to pass Antonelli] was good. I knew I was not going to get many chances. Every lap I spent behind him my chances got lower and lower,” Norris said. “Well played from my part...I probably had one chance.”

News.title: Josko Gvardiol scores in injury time to complete Man City comeback
News.content:
It was a fluid and furious start to Maresca’s Premier League era, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Phil Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising with six defenders, some deployed unexpectedly. Marc Guéhi partnered Elliot Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was in attacking midfield. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines.

Bournemouth showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early onslaught. They have players of class with new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space and time to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

News.title: How to spend a weekend in Lake Garda
News.content:
Lake Garda’s glittering wind-swept waters have long attracted poets, artists, writers and politicians, from DH Lawrence to Wolfgang Goethe – not least Mussolini, who ran the Italian Socialist Republic from the lakefront town of Salò on the western shore.

Fringed by the Dolomites to the north, Italy’s largest lake is Mediterranean both in feel and in flavour, with a mild, temperate climate and a decidedly slow pace of life. Hills are carpeted in olive trees and vineyards, while citrus groves are thick with plump, juicy lemons. In lakefront villages, restaurant tables spill out onto pretty waterfront squares, while boats zip across glimmering waters.

The lower basin is punctuated with sandy coves and gentle rolling hills, while travelling north, the lake takes on a new appearance, with hills replaced by sheer jagged cliffs that plunge into the waters. The northern shore is swept by mountain winds that create the perfect conditions for watersports, with windsailing, kitesurfing, and flyboarding making this a premier destination for outdoor enthusiasts.

News.title: How to spend a perfect weekend in Lake Como
News.content:
An hour drive north of Milan, Lake Como is the most glamorous of Italy’s lakes, hemmed in by the snow-capped Alps with picture-perfect villages on the water. Milanesi pop here for the day for a breath of fresh air and to soak up the fabulous vistas, while international visitors – the Clooneys, the Kennedys – have long been drawn by the grand lakefront hotels and the elegant mahogany Riva boats that zip along the lake’s deep blue waters.

Smart hotels and expensive boats aside, Lake Como is rich in culture, with opulent villas that once belonged to artists, writers, opera singers and explorers. Pliny the Elder, author of the first encyclopaedia, was born here, while 19th-century soprano Giuditta Pasta is known to have entertained composers Bellini and Donizetti in her lakefront residence on the eastern shore.

Though famous spots such as pretty Bellagio still pull in the majority of visitors, the lake has retained its authenticity, with plenty of sleepy fishing villages, such as Laglio, Torno and Nesso, home to rustic, family-run trattorias serving up traditional hearty fare, including risotto al pesce persico (risotto with perch).

News.title: Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair
News.content:
It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

News.title: George Russell king of the sprint and driving with freedom after engagement
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix, the first race after F1’s summer break. Kimi Antonelli has had a tremendous first part of the season, leading Lewis Hamilton by 50 points and George Russell by 59 after the first 11 rounds. He has taken six wins to Russell’s two, with Hamilton, Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc all racking up a win apiece.

His start to the second part of the season was not the best, however. A messy sprint qualifying session meant he ended down in fifth, more than 0.2sec behind team-mate Russell, who took a much-needed pole.

Some of the damage was self-inflicted, quite literally. In the first session of sprint qualifying he ran wide at the banked turn 12 and into the gravel. The damage to the floor of his car was attempted to be repaired for the rest of the session but left him lacking downforce. A gap of 0.2sec is not enormous but the other issue was that three other cars – Norris, Leclerc and Piastri – are between him and Russell.

That said, it is not a great worry at this point. The points available in the sprint are relatively small and Antonelli has a healthy margin at this point over his rivals. In any case, there is no guarantee that Russell and Antonelli finish where they will start. Antonelli has shown on numerous occasions that he can bounce back from a difficult session and you have to expect that again here.

The race, which starts at 11am BST, is one-third of the race distance and should be run in dry conditions. There have been persistent showers and a steady breeze at Zandvoort this weekend, but it is not expected to affect the running in the sprint.

Qualifying for tomorrow’s grand prix comes later today at 3pm, which could be a more consequential session.

Sports.title: Tottenham AGREE Omar Marmoush loan transfer with £50million option to buy after striking deal with Man City
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM have agreed to sign Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush on loan, reports say.

The winger was an unused sub for Enzo Maresca on opening day as his side came from behind to beat Bournemouth.

And Fabrizio Romano claims that a deal with City including a conditional obligation to buy for £50million has been struck just minutes after full-time.



Marmoush, 27, will now travel to London for his medical on Monday.



He will join fellow City attacker Savinho in making the big-money move to Spurs.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men have continued their remarkable summer spending spree with £85million on the Brazilian.

Sports.title: Why are Newcastle and Liverpool players wearing black armbands?
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE and Liverpool kick off their Premier League campaigns with a huge clash at St James’ Park this afternoon.

Both sides are wearing black armbands in memory of footballing great Kevin Keegan.



Why are Newcastle and Liverpool players wearing black armbands?

Players and staff from both Newcastle and Liverpool are wearing black armbands in tribute to Keegan, who died aged 75 in July after a battle with cancer.

Keegan achieved legendary status at both clubs during his illustrious career as both a player and manager.



He scored 100 goals in 322 games during his time on Merseyside, helping Liverpool to three league titles, a European Cup, an FA Cup and two Uefa Cups during his time at the Reds.

Keegan, who won the Ballon d’Or twice during his time at German side Hamburg, ended his playing days at Newcastle.

The former England striker scored 49 times in 85 competitive appearances for the Magpies.

He helped the Toon secure promotion to the First Division in 1983/84 before calling time on his incredible career.



Eight years after retiring on Tyneside, Keegan returned to Newcastle as manager and helped save the club from relegation to the third tier for the first time in the club’s history.

After sealing promotion back to the First Division in his first full season in the St James’ Park dugout, he led the Magpies to the summit of English football.

Before this afternoon’s game, players warmed up in special shirts and a moving display by Wor Flags included both Newcastle and Liverpool supporters.

A minute’s applause also took place prior to kick-off on what will be a very emotional day for all concerned.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace prepare audacious £50m transfer bid to lure Jarrod Bowen back to Premier League amid West Ham nightmare
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE are preparing to launch an audacious £50million bid to lure Jarrod Bowen back to the Premier League.

The West Ham skipper, 29, pledged to stay at the club this season despite relegation to the Championship – and signed a new contract.



But that is not putting off Palace, who are preparing to sell current right winger Ismaila Sarr.

The Hammers’ financial woes are no secret – and selling their captain would go a long way towards easing that pressure.



It would also boost Bowen’s chances of breaking back into the England squad after being overlooked for the World Cup.

Palace, 2-0 opening weekend losers at Everton, want Bowen to replace Sarr, who is keen to leave for Galatasaray.

The Turkish giants are hopeful a £34m switch can be concluded next week.

Senegal winger Sarr, 28, wants Champions League football – and was left out of the Everton game by new Eagles boss Pierre Sage.

Sarr scored 21 goals for Palace last season, helping them win the Conference League.

Bowen managed only 11 in all competitions for West Ham, who went down on the last day of the season.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

His departure would spark a huge fan backlash however as Nuno Espirito Santo’s side are winless in the Championship so far.

Taty Castellanos missed a stoppage-time penalty in yesterday’s 2-1 home defeat to Charlton, with supporters puzzled as to why Bowen did not take it.

Palace were frontrunners to sign Bowen from Hull in January 2020 – but it was West Ham who ended up paying £22m for him that month.

The Eagles will be looking to bounce back from their season-opening defeat to Everton when they face Manchester City on Friday.

Sports.title: Non-league star suffers horror facial fractures and left needing surgery after sickening challenge
Sports.content:
A NON-LEAGUE star is set to go under the knife after suffering a horror facial injury.

Dartford, who hosted a music event to celebrate 20 years at Princes Park, were condemned to a thumping 3-0 defeat by Welling United in the Isthmian Premier League yesterday.



And Joe Tennent had to be substituted in the first half of the Kent minnows’ heavy loss.

The defender, 28, was on the end of a sickening challenge from Welling man Nahum Melvin-Lambert.



Physios rushed to Tennent’s aid after he was immediately seen writhing in agony.

Dartford have shared footage of the incident, which led to Melvin-Lambert escaping with a booking, on social media.

And the Darts have released a statement confirming they are considering taking action as Tennent prepares for an operation.

It read: “Joe sustained displaced facial fractures and will undergo cheekbone reconstruction surgery on Wednesday.

“We wish Joe and his family our very best and a speedy recovery. The club will explore official channels following the incident.”

To make matters worse for Dartford, who have EFL icon Scott Wagstaff on their books, Melvin-Lambert went on to find the net in the second half.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Nathan Cooper and Fumnaya Shomotun were also on target as Welling bagged all three points.

Dartford player-boss Ben Greenhalgh, who won the Champions League with Inter Milan, reckons the injury was a huge turning point.

The ex-Como loanee, 34, said: “I think a really big, key part of today was losing Joe Tennent.

“He’s obviously taken whatever it was to his head. He’s got a possible broken jaw.

“It was a derby game so we knew there were going to be moments. I can’t blame the ref for the game. That has changed it but our second half performance was really poor.



“We lost Joe and I’m not saying we capitulated but we went a bit off-script.

“I am disappointed to lose Joe in that manner. I don’t know how it works from here onwards.

“It didn’t seem like a concussion from what we’re told, but it’s a possible broken jaw that doesn’t sound good at all.”

Sports.title: Man City 2 Bournemouth 1: Josko Gvardiol scores dramatic injury-time winner as Maresca’s men complete late comeback
Sports.content:
NICK it at the death, after a nightmare afternoon.

Maybe Enzo Maresca has got the magic touch needed to deal with the shadow of Pep.



For 84 minutes at the Etihad, Maresca looked like a man who had walked into a deeper pool than he had ever imagined.

Hot on the heels of the embarrassment in Cardiff last week, City looked like a side questioning their new direction.





Self-inflicted blunders, poor selections and a tactical set-up that left many City supporters shaking their heads seemed set to add up to a first opening weekend home defeat since the club returned to the Prem nearly a quarter of a century ago.

Bournemouth, in front through Marcus Tavernier and superbly drilled, were that close to plunging City into further early-season misery.

Yet having got it all wrong from the start, with Marc Guehi an unconvincing midfield screen, Rico Lewis having one to forget and Phil Foden heading down the tunnel when he was hauled off, it all came up trumps for the new City boss.

Guehi had earlier missed an absolute sitter, somehow heading wide of a gaping target from a couple of yards.



That added to a series of misses by Erling Haaland, who had always previously netted on the opening weekend.

But the arrival of Rayan Cherki – making a clear statement when he was belatedly sent on – sparked the stunning turnaround.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

With time running out, it was Cherki’s inswinger from the right that found Guehi on his own, for a header that took a touch off Adrien Truffert on its way into the net.

And three minutes into added time, Cherki teased through, for Josko Gvardiol to find the net.

While the flag was instantly raised, it needed just one replay to signal the inevitable overturned decision, James Hill clearly playing the Croatian onside before he rolled past Djordje Petrovic.



Yet while salvation came in those last few minutes, what had preceded it suggested the burden of replacing a Prem managerial legend may be as tough for Maresca as it proved for David Moyes at United and Unai Emery in North London before him.

For now, the heat will subside. Three points, in any circumstances, tend to have that effect.

Maresca will have his new recruits, too, although expecting £85m teenager Ayyoud Bouaddi to replicate Rodri’s sense of control at the rudder is a big ask.

The Italian, of course, knows he can trust Haaland to come good as well – even if, yesterday at least, the Norwegian did an impression of Samson after Delilah lopped off his flowing locks.

When Haaland, with the goal at his mercy from Nico O’Reilly’s terrific early cross, got it all wrong and the ball bounce off his rib-cage, it was a shock.



Likewise, two second half misses, spooning one over the top and then scuffing a shot when Guehi pulled back, were signals that he is still feeling his way back after his summer exertions in the USA.

That could have been so costly after Bournemouth, with new boss Marco Rise sticking with Andoni Iraola’s set-up and a rope a dope strategy, almost pulled it off perfectly.

When Gigi Donnarumma pawed Rayan’s angled strike behind, it was a warning shot but one they failed to heed.

But when Abdukodir Khusanov barged into Evanilson rather than dealing with Adam Smith’s ball from right-back, the ball to fell to Rayan.



Evanilson, sensing the uncertainty, drifted right to receive and when he slid across, Tavernier had time – so much time, with Lewis horribly out of position – to slam home.

Haaland did force Petrovic to tip over but with Lewis miles off the pace again, it needed Donnarumma’s huge frame to deny Justin Kluivert a second before the interval.

The second half was more about Bournemouth defending yet City remained blunt.

Guehi simply had to score when Petrovic lost his footing from Foden’s corner before after Cherki was sent on, Antoine Semenyo’s low strike was kept out by Petrovic.

Then came those two Haaland misses before the late twist, handing the Cherries their first league defeat since Semenyo left them for City in January.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Maresca will hope that the new recruits ,means his side will get better, too, when they fully understand what is expected of them.

But he cannot keep putting square pegs in round holes and anticipate things all working out. Not in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Newcastle and Liverpool pay tribute to Kevin Keegan as they say goodbye to football legend at Premier League clash
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE and Liverpool came together with a touching tribute to legendary football star Kevin Keegan.

The two-time Ballon d’Or winner sadly died last month after a brave battle with stomach cancer.



Follow the latest updates from Newcastle vs Liverpool on our live blog here

He had been diagnosed with stage four cancer in January after visiting the hospital for abdominal problems.





He passed away surrounded by family at the age of 75, kicking off waves of tributes around the country.

And now Liverpool and the Magpies, both of whom he became a legend for in his playing days, jointly expressed their condolences ahead of their Prem opener on Sunday.

Kenny Dalglish was among the stars to lay a wreath down outside the stadium in honour of his fellow Liverpool legend.

Alan Shearer and Stuart Pearce were also spotted taking in the pre-match tributes from the stands.



St James’ Park itself was filled with handouts featuring Keegan’s name and a heartfelt message from his family.

The stands were also decorated so as to feature his name when empty ahead of the match.



And the matchday programme was dedicated to him, featuring a snap of him as Newcastle manager on the cover.

The Keegan family released a letter to fans before the match that read: “Dear Newcastle United fans and the incredible city of Newcastle.

“The past couple of weeks have been some of the hardest that our family has endured, saying goodbye to our husband, father, and grandfather, Kevin.

“Despite living outside of the region, your love and warmth from the North East has reached our hearts and filled us with so much comfort during these difficult days.



“The empathy, compassion and warmth of this extraordinary club and community have shone through; the outpouring of love has been truly overwhelming.

“Kevin always shared his love for Newcastle United, Geordies, and the city, captivating us with stories told with his infectious smile.

“Seeing these tributes brought those stories to life for Kevin’s grandchildren, showing them how deeply their grandfather was loved in return.

“It also allowed us a quiet moment to reflect on many fond memories of Kevin’s incredible career and the incomparable bond he shared with Newcastle.



“Your football club, city, and community show a passion that truly embodied Kevin as a footballer, manager, and family man. We will be eternally grateful for the adoration and strength you have given our family when we needed it most.”

The players of Liverpool warmed up in kits featuring Keegan’s name and number seven, and a banner featuring his song alongside the word ‘legend’ was placed on the centre circle.



That was accompanied by a tifo featuring a number of photos of Keegan throughout his career as a player and a manager, alongside the caption “King Kev.”

Fans took the opportunity to display their own banners in the stands, including an iconic quote of his.

It read: “I want people to dream about their football club. They should. We should all be dreamers at heart.



“Some people are the opposite and say ‘we can’t do that,’ but when you ask them why, they can’t give a reason. Well I say ‘why not?'”

Manchester City also offered their condolences ahead of their Prem opener with Bournemouth at the Etihad.

Keegan managed the Citizens for four years in the early 2000s, finishing top of the second tier to earn the side promotion back to the Premier League.



Keegan made 230 league appearances for the Reds between 1971 and 1977, winning three first division titles and a European Cup.

He found himself in his native North East a few years later with Newcastle, where he would score 48 times in 78 league appearances in the early 80s.

But he is just as fondly remembered for his managerial career with the club as he is for his playing days.



Eight years after his departure as a player, Keegan returned to kick off his managerial career at St James’ Park, bringing the club back into the top tier under his watch.

There they competed against Manchester United for the Premier League title – and though Keegan never secured silverware with the club, he left a lasting legacy.

The grief of the crowd made the moment all the more spectacular when Anthony Elanga have the home side the lead after just four minutes of play.

The former Nottingham Forest man was released down the right wing by William Osula, and made no mistake firing low across goal to the far post.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick snaps ‘that’s ridiculous’ and gives reporter death stare in tense interview after Man Utd’s loss to Hull
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK snapped “that’s ridiculous” and gave reporter Jan Aage Fjortoft a death stare in a tense interview.

The Manchester United boss suffered the worst-possible start to the new Premier League season.



His dreadful Red Devils side lost 2-0 at newly-promoted Hull City on Saturday.

Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy both scored headers from set pieces in the first half.



And that proved the difference, condemning United to the disaster defeat.

But fuming Carrick rejected suggestions his side lacked passion at the MKM Stadium.



Reporting for Via Play, Fjortoft asked: “I guess in management there are so many buzzwords hanging around like passion, intensity and go for it.

“But would you accept that there was a lack of passion in the first half?”

The new Old Trafford chief was having none of it, though.

He hit back: “Oh, come on.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“That’s ridiculous.”

He then stared at Fjortoft in silence.

After a few awkward moments, the former Swindon, Middlesbrough and Norway striker replied: “That’s not how you will assess it?”

And Carrick doubled down.

He continued: “You played football, you understand.



“That’s a ridiculous thing to say.

“Just because you get beaten, it doesn’t mean you don’t care about it.”

After the ex-footballer tried to defend himself, he asked the same question again about desire.



But Carrick added: “No. Their two goals came from set plays. Other than that, we had opportunities.

“That was where the game was [won and lost].

“I don’t think it was passion or anything to do with that.

“I think it was just their moments that made the difference in the game.”

The bristly exchange came seven months after he was forced to cut short an interview with Fjortoft short after the memorable 3-2 win at Arsenal – because he was summoned to see Sir Jim Ratcliffe.



Incredibly, despite Carrick’s worst day in charge, the 2-0 defeat at Hull could actually be good news for United.

That is because of a spooky 52-year omen.

The last time Hull beat the Red Devils in a league game was in November 1974 – also 2-0 – and they went on to win the league, albeit the Second Division.

Sports.title: Newcastle pay touching tribute to late Kevin Keegan alongside Liverpool as family thank club
Sports.content:
Newcastle pay touching tribute to late Kevin Keegan alongside Liverpool as family thank club

Newcastle United and Liverpool paid tribute to the late Kevin Keegan ahead of their Premier League clash at St James' Park on Sunday, with the family of the legendary manager giving their thanks

View 5 Images Tributes were shown to Kevin Keegan in Newcastle (Image: Sky Sports)

Newcastle United gave a heart-wrenching tribute to the late Kevin Keegan at St James' Park on Sunday afternoon ahead of their Premier League opener with Liverpool. The legendary former footballer and manager died at the age of 75 last month following a battle with cancer, with tributes pouring in across the world of sport.

‌



And given the Armthorpe-born icon represented the Magpies both as a player and a manager, as well as Liverpool during his playing days, the clubs felt it was only right that they afforded him an emotional send-off ahead of their first English top flight outing of 2026/27.

‌



On top of the players warming up in shirts adorned with Keegan's iconic number seven, 500 shirts were laid in a mosaic reading 'legend' and 'There's only one Kevin Keegan,' in the centre circle of the stadium. Bobby Moncur, Ian Rush, Shola Ameobi and Sir Kenny Dalglish also laid wreaths in the Newcastle memorial gardens ahead of Sunday's 4.30pm kick-off on Tyneside.

‌



Kevin Keegan's cause of death as Liverpool and Newcastle prepare to pay tribute READ MORE :

A letter from Keegan's family was also included in the pre-match programme, in which fans were thanked for their support over an incredibly tough period. It read: "Dear Newcastle United fans and the incredible city of Newcastle.

"The past couple of weeks have been some of the hardest that our family has endured, saying goodbye to our husband, father, and grandfather, Kevin. Despite living outside of the region, your love and warmth from the North East has reached our hearts and filled us with so much comfort during these difficult days.

"The empathy, compassion and warmth of this extraordinary club and community have shone through; the outpouring of love has been truly overwhelming. Having seen the tributes outside St. James’ Park, members of our family came home to Newcastle to see the memorials in person.

‌



"The sea of black and white shirts and scarves, alongside colours from so many other clubs, reminded us how much Kevin meant to the footballing world. It was a sombre moment that reminded us of our pain and loss, yet matched with immense pride and love as we read so many personal and heartfelt messages.

"Kevin always shared his love for Newcastle United, Geordies, and the city, captivating us with stories told with his infectious smile. Seeing these tributes brought those stories to life for Kevin’s grandchildren, showing them how deeply their grandfather was loved in return.

"It also allowed us a quiet moment to reflect on many fond memories of Kevin’s incredible career and the incomparable bond he shared with Newcastle. Your football club, city, and community show a passion that truly embodied Kevin as a footballer, manager, and family man.

View 5 Images Former Newcastle and Liverpool players laid wreathes (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



"We will be eternally grateful for the adoration and strength you have given our family when we needed it most. Newcastle, thank you for your love. The Keegan Family."

Placards were also left on seats around St James' Park for fans to hold up in the build-up to kick-off, adorned with instructions and the words "Long live the king." Wor Flags also provided a display of Keegan's name in red in the Liverpool section of Level Seven, while the number seven sat below among the home fans.

View 5 Images Placards were left for fans inside St James' Park (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The Newcastle-based organisation also erected a one-off tifo which showed a collage of Keegan from his time at Newcastle United as both a player and a manager, as well as the words "King Kev." Meanwhile, fans held banners in the stands, showing Keegan's iconic "we should all be dreamers message."

A minute of applause was also given for Keegan as kick-off fast approached, with both sets of supporters, as well as the likes od Dalglish and Alan Shearer joining in. A two-time Ballon d'Or winner, Keegan kicked off his footballing career at Scunthorpe United in 1968, spending three years with the club before a move to Liverpool arrived.

View 5 Images Newcastle and Liverpool fans paid tribute to Keegan (Image: Sky Sports)

‌



After spending six years with the Reds, he moved onto Hamburger SV, before returning to English soil with Southampton in 1980. Keegan arrived at St James' Park in 2982, enjoying a two-year stint with the club before seeing out the last year of his career at Blacktown City.

In a trophy-laden playing career, Keegan won the First Division title with Liverpool three times, as well as the European Cup and a pair of UEFA Cups. He also won a Bundesliga title with Hamburg. Keegan then stepped into the world of management in 1992 with Newcastle, guiding the club to a First Division (now Championship) title in his maiden season.

View 5 Images Keegan was a club legend for Newcastle and Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

After five years at the helm, Keegan moved onto Fulham for two years, and enjoyed short stints with England and manchester-city-fc>Manchester City before one last dance with the Magpies in 2008.

Rest in peace, Kevin.

Sports.title: Aston Villa's overhaul exposed as Unai Emery's new era has worst possible start
Sports.content:
Aston Villa's overhaul exposed as Unai Emery's new era has worst possible start

BRIGHTON 4-0 ASTON VILLA: Unai Emery's new look side endured the worst possible start to their Premier League season as they were hammered on the south coast

View 2 Images Unai Emery's new look Aston Villa side were destroyed at Brighton

If you're going to sell six of the XI who helped you win a first trophy in 30 years, then you'd better show why. Aston Villa's opening game only served to suggest that the timing of their mass overhaul may have been a little premature.

‌



Unai Emery stood on the touchline at the Amex and saw his Europa League champions trailing 4-0 inside 31 minutes. His defence, minus Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, were the architects of their own downfall. Brighton were able to take advantage of Villa giving the ball away in their own box to score two of their four goals.

‌



Emery could not rely on Youri Tielemans to get control of the game - he's gone. He couldn't turn to Morgan Rogers to try and produce a moment of individual magic - he's gone.

‌



Emery couldn't ask Ollie Watkins to run in behind and stretch the Brighton defence - he was left out and looks like he's off to Saudi Arabia.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The succession planning beyond Watkins is not exactly in place. There's talk of a move for Nicolas Jackson, but with Watkins omitted, Emery had to start with no recognised No.9 in his line-up. Emi Buendia was tasked with leading the line.

‌



Joao Gomes, the man who is serving as the replacement for Tielemans, didn't even last 45 minutes as he was shown a red card on debut.

By the time he was dismissed the game was effectively over. Victor Lindelof, who started less than a third of games last term and would likely be on the bench if Konsa was still present, put through his own net inside 10 minutes. Maxim De Cuyper tapped home to double the Brighton lead and Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in two minutes, which saw some Villa fans in the away end head for the exits.

View 2 Images Aston Villa have lost more than half of last year's team, raising questions over the timing of their overhaul

‌



Villa's summer business has been in part driven by a need to remain financially compliant. That said, rarely, if ever, has history shown that ripping up a team who finished fourth and won a European trophy is a good idea, especially in the short term.

We haven't even mentioned Emi Martinez, who was left out after another summer where he's been linked with the exit door. The Argentine's move to Juventus fell through recently and Villa have already moved for life after Martinez, signing Zion Suzuki from Parma.

Before kick-off, Emery claimed his Villa side were "motivated, we are so excited". It must be said that the Midlands outfit have suffered opening weekend hammerings in the past - losing 5-1 at Newcastle in 2023 before going on to finish fourth.

Article continues below

That was under very different circumstances though and with a team that enjoyed continuity. Emery is the one constant at Villa, and the Spaniard has continually outperformed his resources at Villa Park, but those resources may have been gutted to an extent that even his magic wand is limited.

Sports.title: Barcelona make Alejandro Balde decision after Man Utd boss Michael Carrick drops hint
Sports.content:
Barcelona make Alejandro Balde decision after Man Utd boss Michael Carrick drops hint

Alejandro Balde wants to leave Barcelona before the transfer window closes and he's been linked with joining Manchester United amid their search for a left-back

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde is a target for Manchester United (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Manchester United target Alejandro Balde has been left out of Barcelona's squad for their La Liga opener against Elche. Balde, 22, is on the Camp Nou chopping block and wants to secure a move away ahead of the transfer window closing on September 1.

‌



The Spaniard is an option for United, who are scouring the market for a left-back. Talks have reportedly been held with Balde's agent, Jorge Mendes, with the Red Devils preparing a bid of €40million (£34m).

‌



On Sunday, Barcelona announced their 25-man travelling squad to face Elche and Balde wasn't included. Marc Casado and Hector Fort were also left out, with all three players up for sale.

‌



Both Balde and Fort's chances of game time took a hit this week when Barca welcomed back Joao Cancelo, who can play on the left and right-hand side of defence. Cancelo's arrival on loan in January led to a reduction in minutes for Balde, whose 2025-26 campaign was also blighted by hamstring injuries.

Barca boss Hansi Flick hailed the 22-year-old in his pre-match press conference but isn't sure whether he can compete with Cancelo. "He's a player of immense quality, and it's important to know if he's confident he can compete in his position," Flick said.

"That's what I want to see from all my players. Every day I observe what they do, their level, whether they demonstrate that they're at the level to play."

Flick's comments come after Michael Carrick was quizzed on United's left-back search before they started the Premier League season with a limp 2-0 loss away to newly promoted Hull. "I just think we're looking to strengthen the squad," Carrick replied.

"So, yeah, certainly trying to make the most of the opportunities to finish the window stronger than we went into it. And I think we're a good way to doing that, so far."

Lewis Hall of Newcastle was United's top left-back target earlier in the window, but he's seen as unattainable this summer for a variety of reasons. Newcastle don't need to sell and have already lost three key players, while United have spent most of their budget on midfielders.

Sports.content:
Erling Haaland makes major change as Man City star reveals surprise new look

Erling Haaland is sporting a fresh new look and surprised the likes of Pep Guardiola, Noel Gallagher and Zlatan Ibrahimovic after cutting his long blond locks

View 5 Images Erling Haaland is sporting a brand new look for the 2026/27 Premier League season (Image: Instagram/Erling)

Erling Haaland has debuted a jaw-dropping new hairstyle ahead of Manchester City's Premier League curtain-raiser against Bournemouth. His flowing blond mane is gone, replaced by a sharp, buzz cut, much to the surprise of the likes of Pep Guardiola and Jack Grealish.

‌



Haaland shared a series of snaps documenting his trip to the barber's chair, giving followers a full reveal of the finished result. There were perhaps a few raised eyebrows when Haaland initially unveiled a curtains-style cut midway through the session.

‌



However, the end product was a neat finish that will lighten the load up top. The Premier League superstar took to Instagram with two posts to show off his new look, declaring: "Short hair, don't care" and "New season, new trim."

‌



Haaland has also uploaded a YouTube video capturing the whole experience. At the outset, he said: "This beautiful blond hair, time to let it go.

Sports.title: Man City eye Rodri replacement as Enzo Maresca highlights successful transfer plan
Sports.content:
Man City eye Rodri replacement as Enzo Maresca highlights successful transfer plan

Manchester City have already signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest this summer but it appears that Enzo Maresca still wants more additions ahead of the transfer window closing

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca has hinted more signings could be on the way at Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca has underlined his desire to find the ‘next Rodri’ ahead of next month’s transfer deadline. The Spanish midfielder left Manchester City earlier this week in a big-money switch to Barcelona.

‌



It brought to an end a glittering seven-year spell for Rodri at the Etihad Stadium, where he helped the club to numerous Premier League titles, the Champions League, as well as claiming the Ballon d’Or for himself.

‌



City have already made a big-money addition in the heart of midfield with a £116million move for England star Elliot Anderson. But it appears that they are not done there, with talks underway with Lille for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

‌



Regardless of who is drafted in, Maresca has suggested that they are looking for someone with a similar profile to Rodri. And while the City boss is aware of the enormity of that task, he believes it’s something that they’ve managed to navigate before.

"How do we solve that problem?" asked Maresca. "We try to find the new Rodri, it is what it is.

"[Before] Rodri arrived here, he didn't win the Ballon d'Or, he didn't win the Champions League, he didn't win the Club World Cup. He joined the club then he achieved many important things."

Sports.content:
Man Utd fans think they've discovered reason for Hull defeat as comments resurface

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick and his players are facing heavy criticism after slipping to a 2-0 loss against Hull in their first game of the new Premier League season

View Image Youri Tielemans' comments in pre-season have taken on new meaning (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Concerned Manchester United supporters have pointed to comments made by new signing Youri Tielemans following their disastrous start to the Premier League season. United suffered a humiliating 2-0 defeat away to newly promoted Hull, who went into the 2026-27 campaign as favourites to finish bottom.

‌



The Red Devils' failure to defend two set pieces proved to be their downfall, but fans and pundits alike pointed to fitness levels as another factor in the defeat. United looked lethargic all over the pitch, with new midfield duo Andrey Santos and Tielemans - who cost a combined £85m - particularly coming in for criticism.

‌



"They didn't look fit," Alan Shearer declared on BBC Radio 5 Live. "They didn't look ready to play 90 minutes of intense, high pressure, high energy football."

‌



After the match, Tielemans' interview with United legend Rio Ferdinand resurfaced on social media. The chat was recorded in pre-season shortly after the 29-year-old had joined from Aston Villa.

When Ferdinand asked if the squad had done 'loads of running', the Belgian replied: "No, when you come back from the World Cup, you just chill."

"What?" a surprised Ferdinand said. It's worth noting that Tielemans was only involved in the latter stages of United's pre-season, having been at the World Cup before signing for the Red Devils.

Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi 'knew last week' that Tottenham had major issue before Brentford mauling

Big-spending Tottenham suffered an abject 3-0 loss away to Brentford on Saturday in their Premier League opener, but Roberto De Zerbi saw the warning signs long before

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi wasn't surprised by Tottenham's defeat to Brentford (Image: Hayters TV)

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi has revealed he 'knew last week' that his side were in for a reality check against Brentford. Spurs were hammered 3-0 by the Bees and it would've been more had Igor Thiago not missed a penalty.

‌



After spending £228million in the summer transfer window and with more signings still to come which will take them to nearly £350m, Tottenham have been tipped to vastly improve on their back-to-back 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. The result came as a shock to many - but not De Zerbi.

‌



"I knew before the game, I knew from last Saturday when we played against Hoffenheim, we are not at the right point in terms of physical condition for a lot of reasons," the Spurs boss confessed.

‌



"For the players, they came after the World Cup and they came late for the pre-season in Australia where we had not time to work in the right way, in the best way, but it's not an excuse.

Alexander Isak was the subject of a brutal welcome on his return to Newcastle ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Liverpool

View 2 Images Alexander Isak is back in Newcastle for Liverpool's season opener at St James' Park (Image: Getty Images)

Alexander Isak was greeted with a torrent of boos and foul-mouthed abuse upon his return to Newcastle, a year after his contentious switch to Liverpool. In what proved to be the most compelling saga of last summer's transfer window, the Swedish frontman sealed a £125million deadline day move to Anfield.

‌



While Eddie Howe had been confident that Isak would remain at St. James' Park for the 2025/26 season, the striker sent shockwaves through Tyneside by declaring his desire to seek opportunities elsewhere. What followed was over a month of turmoil, during which the 26-year-old snubbed Newcastle United's pre-season tour, opting instead to train with former club Real Sociedad.

‌



On his return to Darsley Park, he was excluded from first-team training as he pushed for his desired move to Merseyside. That wish was ultimately granted on September 1, when Liverpool confirmed a British record fee for the centre-forward.

‌



Liverpool star told he must tear up his contract to seal return to former club READ MORE :

The devoted Toon Army faithful, who had worshipped Isak for nearly three years, swiftly turned on their former hero; social media erupted with insults, while others went as far as unfurling a banner outside Newcastle's ground reading 'Isak is a pure rat.'

On Saturday, Isak made his highly-anticipated return to the North East ahead of Sunday's showdown between Liverpool and Newcastle, where he was met, as widely predicted, by incensed supporters gathered outside the Reds' team hotel. Footage circulating online shows Isak calmly walking through the hotel entrance, shutting out a barrage of boos and abuse with his earphones in.

Newcastle supporters could be heard shouting the likes of "F*** off," and "W*****" in the clip, as their former hero strode past, expressionless and apparently unmoved by the hostility.

‌



View 2 Images Alexander Isak received a hostile welcome on his return to Newcastle.

A comparable welcome awaits the striker when he steps out at St. James' on Sunday afternoon, with the two sides due to clash in an explosive Premier League curtain-raiser at 4.30pm.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌

Isak will be eager to silence the bulk of the 52,719 supporters packed inside the stadium during the 90 minutes, anticipated to spearhead Andoni Iraola's attack with Hugo Ekitike still out following an Achilles tendon rupture earlier this year.

This follows a rollercoaster debut campaign on Merseyside for the centre-forward, largely disrupted by his own fitness struggles. Having missed pre-season due to his protracted transfer, Isak wasn't given the chance to make an immediate impact with the Reds, as then-manager Arne Slot cautiously monitored his condition.

‌



Isak's season was further derailed in late December when he suffered a fractured leg during a 2-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur. The injury sidelined Isak for a total of 106 days, with adductor problems and muscular issues forcing him to miss another two fixtures towards the campaign's conclusion.

Isak netted only three goals from 14 appearances in total, but will be aiming for a more consistent campaign in 2026/27, beginning with an awkward return to Newcastle.

Sports.title: Norris beats Antonelli to victory in Dutch GP
Sports.content:
Lando Norris outduelled championship leader Kimi Antonelli to claim his second successive race victory by winning the Dutch Grand Prix.

McLaren's Norris started on pole in Zandvoort but lost the lead to Antonelli at an early standing restart after Red Bull's Max Verstappen triggered a red flag at his home race by crashing out at the end of the first lap.

After struggling to pressure Antonelli on the first stint, Norris was far quicker after switching onto a hard tyre at the first round of pit stops, and eventually passed the Mercedes after emerging from his second stop with far fresher tyres than the Italian.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen loses control of his car at the beginning of the race and hits the wall

Mercedes ordered George Russell to let Antonelli through to second in the closing stages, and he was only just able to hold off Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton for the final podium spot.

Antonelli's championship lead grows to 59 points with Russell taking over second from Hamilton in the standings, while Norris reduces his deficit to the leader to 83 points.

Sports.title: Aventure ends Diamond Necklace's unbeaten record
Sports.content:
Diamond Necklace tasted defeat for the first time as Aventure served up a reminder of her top-class credentials in the Sumbe Prix Jean et Louis Romanet at Deauville.

Aidan O'Brien's daughter of St Mark's Basilica was expected to dazzle once again in France, as she had done when landing the Prix Marcel Boussac, Poule d'Essai Des Pouliches and Prix de Diane on her travels during what was an unbeaten six-race career to date.

However, she had no answer to the experience of her Christophe Ferland-trained elder, who added to last year's Group One strike in the Prix Vermeille and earned herself a quote of 20/1 for another crack at the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe from bookmakers, a race in which she finished second to Bluestocking in 2024.

In a close-up third was the Charlie Johnston-trained Timeforshowcasing, who ran a big race in the hands of Jack Mitchell.

More to follow...

Senorita Bonita proves jet-propelled in Prix Morny

Senorita Bonita demonstrated her devastating turn of foot to scorch to Sumbe Prix Morny glory.

The 900,000 guineas top lot from April's Craven Breeze-Up sale, Simon and Ed Crisford's filly arrived on the Normandy coast looking to follow up her victory in Newmarket's Duchess of Cambridge Stakes, a win that received a timely boost by Lowther Stakes scorer Libertango earlier this week.

Held up towards the rear by Oisin Murphy, with Clive Cox's Royal Ascot winner Orthodox ahead, the daughter of Starspangledbanner had plenty of ground to make up on Aidan O'Brien's front-running Carry The Flag entering the final third of the contest.

However, once the champion jockey stepped on the accelerator the response was instant, as not only did Senorita Bonita rapidly eat away at the deficit but then surged readily clear of the long-time pace-setter for a thoroughly impressive victory.

Simon Crisford said: "She's shown a great turn of front and obviously they set some very good fractions up front but she finished off super well - she galloped out strongly.

"She was a little bit slow out of the gates and behind the bridle early, but they were going quick and the race set up for the closers and she was the best of the closers.

Image: Winning rider Oisin Murphy with Senorita Bonita

"At halfway I briefly thought we might have a mountain to climb here, but she's got such a good turn of foot that at the furlong pole you could see she was going to come home strong."

It was the father and son training team's second victory in the Group One race after Vandeek in 2023, while it continues the fine record of fillies in the contest following on from Venetian Sun's triumph for Karl Burke 12 months ago.

The Victorious Racing-owned Senorita Bonita will now go in search of further top honours in Newmarket's Cheveley Park Stakes and was made 5/2 by bookmakers for a race where she could meet former foe Libertango once again, as well as another recent York winner, Sun Goddess.

"All roads lead to the Cheveley Park now at the end of September and that was a fantastic performance," continued Crisford.

"It was a deep, deep renewal and it was a really, really pleasing effort and she's looked really impressive there.

"Any Group One is fantastic to win and we are all just delighted. It's a great testament to the staff back at home and everyone involved and it's great to win for Shaikh Nasser (bin Hamed Al Khalifa) and Shaikh Khalid (bin Hamed Al Khalifa)."

Sports.title: Nightmare start! Aston Villa concede four first-half goals in thumping by Brighton
Sports.content:
Aston Villa produced one of the worst opening 45 minutes in Premier League history on their way to a heavy 4-0 defeat at Brighton.

Unai Emery's side, who were without a recognised centre forward with Ollie Watkins left out of the squad amid interest from Saudi club Al Hilal, conceded FOUR goals in an extraordinary 31 minutes of football before Joao Gomes capped a nightmare Villa league debut by being shown a straight red card just before the interval.

It all came after a bright start from Emery's side with Emi Buendia, who was playing as Villa's most advanced forward, having three efforts on goal inside the first 10 minutes, but that was where any hope ended for the visitors as Brighton went on to run riot in the first half.

Maxim De Cuyper latched onto Pau Torres' poor pass before squeezing his shot in via the post and Victor Lindelof as Brighton took the lead through an own goal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pau Torres' wayward back-pass gifts Brighton an early lead against Aston Villa

De Cuyper then got himself on the scoresheet 10 minutes later after converting Georginio Rutter's cross before Jack Hinshelwood's quickfire double (30, 31) sent Brighton to dreamland.

Villa's first-half collapse was complete five minutes before the break as new signing Gomes, who had already been booked, was sent off after a VAR review for a kick out at Rutter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joao Gomes has a debut to forget after being shown a second yellow in the first half for Aston Villa

It capped a first half to forget for both Gomes and Villa, but Emery's side managed to stem the flow of goals in the second half, limiting the damage of what proved to be a costly first-half collapse.

But after a turbulent summer at Villa Park, which has seen key players Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne leave the club, this is a damaging opening defeat for Villa, leaving plenty of questions for Emery to answer with just over a week left of the summer transfer window.

The key moments from Villa's first half collapse at the Amex Stadium...

8: GOAL! De Cuyper latches onto Torres' poor pass before squeezing his shot into the back of the net via the post and Lindelof!

18: GOAL! De Cuyper gets on the scoresheet, converting Rutter's cross to double Brighton's lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maxim De Cuyper taps home Brighton's second goal against Aston Villa inside 20 minutes

30: GOAL! Hinshelwood heads home from close range to continue Brighton's dream start.

31: GOAL! Less than a minute and 20 seconds later, Hinshelwood grabs a second to inflict more pain on Villa.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack Hinshelwood scores a rapid-fire double to make it FOUR for Brighton in the first half against Aston Villa

40: RED CARD! Villa's first half goes from bad to worse as Gomes is shown a red card for kicking out at Rutter.

Aston Villa became only the second team in Premier League history to concede four goals, receive a red card and score an own goal in the first half of a match, after Southampton against Manchester United in February 2021.



Meanwhile, Brighton are only the fourth side to score four goals in the first half of their opening game of a Premier League season, after Bolton in 2001/02 (vs Leicester), Manchester United in 2006/07 (vs Fulham), and Liverpool in 2019/20 (vs Norwich).

Your views: 'Villa's recruitment has been shocking'

Image: Victor Lindelof reacts after Aston Villa fall 4-0 behind to Brighton

Jake: I thought Aston Villa were in for a slow start but not to this extent. The recruitment has been shocking. You don't sell your best players and expect to be fine.

Jack: Not even a Villa fan but that might be the worst start to a season ever from a team expected to be in and around European spots - feel for the fans that travelled down there for that. A hard one to take.

Alex: Brilliant Brighton performance so far but isn't this a perfect example of how bad the financial rules in football are? Villa won a European trophy and qualified for the Champions League yet their squad has been torn apart this summer and this is what they've got left...

Jamie: Villa have sold Emery's team from under him and not replaced them. This was almost an inevitability. It's barely a shock. I think Emery could end up walking if they don't recruit in the coming days.

Mikey: What a horror show for the Villains! The worst performance of the weekend, in a sea of bad performances by top sides!

THAV22: Worst possible start to the season. No recognised striker, players have not been replaced who were sold, awful debut from Gomes.

Bennett 69: An absolute shambles. We are selling all our best players. We just look devoid of any ideas.

'Emery needs clarity over Villa squad'

Image: Joao Gomes is sent off by referee Peter Bankes

Sky Sports' Lee Hendrie at the Amex Stadium:

"The damage was done in the first half by Brighton.

"The only positive Aston Villa can take from this is they didn't concede a goal in the second half.

"However, it was a frustrating afternoon for Unai Emery. He will now just want some certainty over who will be at the football club come the end of the transfer window.

"It must be so difficult for him, at the moment because the transfer window is all he is being asked about. It's a big distraction for Aston Villa."

Emery at a loss to explain Villa's first-half collapse

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery:

"We started the first 10-15 minutes very well. Then I can't understand exactly why we lost in 20 minutes all the match and a player.

"But this is the process we have. We know football is not easy, we know four years working here in Villa we have to work in difficult moments as well. Always we recover a good moment. Always came back, with the situation maybe like we have now.

"The response on the field in the second half, I'm really happy.

"The players they didn't give up, they worked it, showed good commitment and kept going."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Unai Emery was short of words when asked about the future of Ollie Watkins

McGinn apologises to Villa fans - but proud of second-half reaction

Aston Villa captain John McGinn to Sky Sports:

"We started the game very well. Had the chance to go ahead with Emi [Buendia]. We were the ones to create the chances. But playing at the highest level, when you make a mistake, they happen. The goals we concded were poor, there's no getting away from that.

"Going away in the Premier League, we obviously apologise to the supporters, it's not easy to travel, costs a lot of money, takes a lot of time. And they don't want to come here and see their team lose by four goals before half-time. But on the flipside, 4-0 down at the Amex with 10 men, we had to stand up in the second half and the squad of players in there, we had a chance to puff our chests out, be men and fight and we did that.

"We're obviously angry and disappointed at the result. We set high standards and that's far away from that. However, there's a bit of me that's proud at how we reacted. Today could easily have got away from us and got messy. A lot of pride in the second-half performance. After five games last season, we had one point. Hopefully this season can go the same way as that."

Hurzeler pleased with 'nice goals' and Brighton performance

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler:

"[What did he like most?] Clean sheet!

"The first minutes we struggled a little bit. But then more and more we got the control of the game back. We scored some nice goals. The first goal with some luck. But we scored some nice goals that helped our game, the intensity. The red card was a gamechanger but all the goals we scored were 11 v 11.

"The second half we were quite serious. We had the ball, controlled the game, didn't give away the ball too easy and created some chances. Quite a mature performance.

"It's always helpful to win games. But it was only one game. A good start. Now we have another big challenge ahead of us on Thursday."

Hinshelwood praises Brighton intensity Brighton midfielder Jack Hinshelwood to Sky Sports:



"We started the game really well. We brought that energy, intensity. We were very deserving of our four goals and it was a professional performance from that point on.



"You can do all the tactics you want in the week but if you don't bring that energy and passion to go and press it means nothing. We got that spot on."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Price double gives West Brom turnaround win over Burnley
Sports.content:
Isaac Price inspired West Bromwich Albion to a 3-1 comeback win against promotion favourites Burnley in the Sky Bet Championship.

The Northern Ireland international scored twice in the second half at The Hawthorns after setting up Harry Whitwell's equaliser to cancel out Callum Styles' own goal.

Burnley, without star striker Zian Flemming with a calf injury amid interest from Lille, failed to match their lofty billing in a disappointing second-half display.

After the loss, Burnley boss Nicky Hayen could not confirm whether Flemming would stay at the club before the window closes on September 1.

He told Sky Sports: "If there is an offer that suits the finances of the club, then maybe the transfer can be done, but I want him to stay.

"Everyone has the ambition to play in the Premier League, so if he can make that step then okay, everything should be in place, but as long as that's not the case, Zian stays with us."

Albion continued their 100 per cent start to the season, gaining their third straight win in all competitions and second in the league to lie second in the early table behind Millwall on goal difference.

But Burnley suffered their first defeat of the campaign as new boss Nicky Hayen still awaits his first Championship win.

How West Brom maintained perfect start

Image: Isaac Price hit a double in West Brom's win

In a fast and furious start, there were two goals in the first 18 minutes.

Styles put into his own net in the eighth minute from Jacob Bruun Larsen's cross. Albion complained that Hannibal Mejbri fouled Felix Horn Myhre in the build-up some 70 yards away, with several passages of play unfolding before the goal.

Whitwell equalised in the 18th minute when he slotted home low to Max Weiss' left from 12 yards for the 20-year-old's first Albion league goal.

But it was Burnley who went closest to scoring again when Bruun Larsen sidefooted against the foot of the post from Marcus Edwards' searching cross.

It was a different story after the break. Inspired by Price, Albion produced a dominant second-half performance, with the perfect start.

Price put them ahead for the first time, in the 46th minute, curling the ball beyond Weiss, who had strayed five yards off his line, into the far corner.

Burnley made a triple change in the 57th minute with the arrival of Ugo Raghouber, Zeki Amdouni, and Dastan Satpayev.

Instead, it was Albion who struck next to effectively seal it, after Bashir Humphreys upended Whitwell for a clear penalty.

Price made no mistake from the spot, firing low to Weiss's right with the 'keeper going the wrong way.

Morrison not getting carried out with perfect start

West Brom boss James Morrison speaking to Sky Sports:

"When you start the pre-season and see the fixtures come out and see the opposition you're like, 'Oof, welcome back!'

"But it was an opportunity to impose ourselves, and we've been doing that, and it's my job to keep us firmly on the ground.

"It's been two games, and it's going to be a long, hard season with ups and downs, but we've got to keep working hard on the training pitch and see what happens."

Hayen: Defeat totally deserved

Burnley boss Nicky Hayen speaking to Sky Sports:

"It was totally deserved. They had much more energy than us, winning duels and second balls.

"We played too slowly and were far away from the level last week.

"If we play at our best, we're a top team, but if you play like this, you're an average team, and we have to go back to what we did last week because today we weren't good enough."

Sports.title: ECB investigating as Carse handcuffed by police outside Derby nightclub
Sports.content:
England fast bowler Brydon Carse seen in handcuffs outside nightclub in Derby in video circulating on social media; Carse set to be in England squad for second Pakistan Test starting on Thursday at Lord's

Brydon Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby

The ECB is investigating an incident involving England player Brydon Carse, after footage emerged showing the bowler handcuffed by police outside a Derby nightclub on Saturday night.

In a statement to Sky Sports News, the ECB confirmed is it aware of the incident.

A video obtained by The Telegraph shows Carse with police, with a Durham team-mate talking to him. Former England captain Ben Stokes is also pictured.

According to The Telegraph, Carse was briefly detained by police but not arrested. He returned to the team hotel soon after and it is unclear what led the police placing him in handcuffs.

Carse was part of England's squad for the first Test against Pakistan at Headingley but was not in the starting XI, so was released to play for his county.

The Division Two leaders comfortably beat Derbyshire, with Carse taking two wickets and Stokes taking a five-for.

Carse was set to be part of the squad for England's second Test vs Pakistan, which begins at Lord's on Thursday. The team will assemble in London on Monday.

Sky Sports News has contacted Derbyshire Police and the Cricket Regulator for comment.

More to follow...
