Sports.title: Verstappen suffering from "flu-like" illness as Zandvoort exposes Red Bull's fundamental problems
Sports.content:
With three victories since the Dutch Grand Prix returned to the calendar in 2021, Max Verstappen can already look back on a very successful period. The final edition in 2026 has proven an ordeal so far, both in terms of Red Bull’s pace and Verstappen’s physical condition.

"I've felt better before, yes," Verstappen admitted during the Dutch media session in the paddock after qualifying. "I feel a bit flu-like and I’m just not feeling as much energy as normal."

Asked whether that also affects his performance behind the wheel, he continued: "No, I don’t think so. I think once you’re in the car, it’s actually fine."

It does mean Verstappen is experiencing his final home race somewhat differently and is mainly looking forward to the moment he can get some rest: "Of course I still enjoy all the fans in the grandstands, but apart from that, I’m mostly looking forward to getting some sleep."

Why Zandvoort exposes some fundamental Red Bull problems

Aside from Verstappen’s physical condition, Red Bull is also struggling for performance at the circuit in the dunes. The home hero had to settle for seventh on the grid and was more than four tenths behind polesitter Lando Norris in qualifying.

"We changed quite a lot on the car after the sprint, but none of it made any difference," Verstappen said when asked by Autosport.

According to Verstappen, the Zandvoort circuit exposes some of Red Bull’s weaknesses to an exaggerated degree Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

"The balance of the car is the biggest problem. It’s just not consistent throughout the entire corner, but it has been like that all season. It’s just a little worse at some circuits than at others."

In that respect, Zandvoort is a track that exposes the RB22’s weaknesses more than most.

"It depends on the tarmac sometimes, but also on the layout of the track. This one is for sure not our best layout, but we just need to work on it. We can guess on what track it might be a little bit better, but we need to try and just dial it out."

Verstappen added that, in his view, it is not so much related to set-up, as Red Bull has tried everything in that respect: "I think we’re now simply more limited by some fundamental problems with the car that we need to solve.

"At this circuit you also have some fast corners and we’re lacking there as well. In general, if you don’t have a good balance, you can’t really attack the corners. And if you don’t have traction either, you can’t get out of the corners properly, so all of that costs time."

It means Verstappen considers seventh place the maximum achievable result on Sunday under normal circumstances, particularly if there is no chaos caused by rain.

Without rain, Verstappen reckons that P7 will be the best he can hope for in his final home race Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

It may not be the Zandvoort farewell he had hoped for, although the four-time world champion stresses that the Dutch GP era as a whole has already been a great success.

"It’s absolutely the end of an era," he said. "To have had your own home race and to have been able to win it a few times is very special. Of course, it’s a shame that it’s going away, but on the other hand, it has also given me a lot of great moments and memories."

Whether another memorable moment will be added remains to be seen, but Verstappen took a pragmatic view in conclusion.

"I’m really only satisfied when we win, but that’s going to be very difficult tomorrow," he said. "We’ve been a little too slow throughout this season and that’s not suddenly going to change in Zandvoort, but we’re just going to try to enjoy it one last time."

Sports.title: Why Verstappen's 2026 Mercedes contact was very different from last year's
Sports.content:
Will Max Verstappen ever race for Mercedes in Formula 1? This is what team principal Toto Wolff is quizzed about in his yearly media session with Dutch journalists at Zandvoort – and this time the door looks closed, though Wolff keeps it ever so slightly ajar.

F1’s history could have panned out very differently if Mercedes had beaten Red Bull to secure the youngster’s future back in 2014, as Verstappen kept winning races in Formula 3 as a single-seater rookie, but his sights were firmly set on an immediate world championship debut. That’s something only Red Bull could offer, courtesy of its second outfit.

Since then, Mercedes and Verstappen have always been rivals, but two years ago, Wolff revealed he had held talks with the then-three-time world champion. The Austrian faced the tall order of finding a worthy replacement for Ferrari-bound Lewis Hamilton and had already set his sights on next-generation wunderkind Kimi Antonelli, but he obviously wouldn’t have passed on the opportunity of recruiting Verstappen, had it had the slightest chance of materialising.

It didn’t, but Wolff insisted the door was not closed, when asked by Autosport if a potential move for Verstappen was still in the back of his mind: “Yes, it is. Somehow I have that feeling. But I don't know when that could be. Whether it's '26, whether it's three years later, I don't know yet.”

Wolff again sounded out Verstappen one year later, as rookie Antonelli struggled in his maiden season, but the Red Bull racer pledged loyalty anew to the Milton Keynes-based team.

“Could that mean our paths will never cross because the timings are wrong? Well, that can happen,” Wolff pondered at the time. “But that could be 50%. The other 50% is we are racing together at a certain stage in our careers, if it is right for both sides.”

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

But by now, Wolff admits he can’t see Verstappen joining Mercedes anytime soon, after Russell and Antonelli were confirmed in the Silver Arrows for 2027 back in June, while the Dutchman’s new Red Bull deal was announced ahead of his home race – despite Verstappen currently going through his first winless campaign since 2015.

“Pretty early we felt for us that being with George and Kimi was the right decision to continue – for various reasons, but it seems that the driver line-up is just the right positive dynamic,” Wolff commented. “It allows Kimi to grow and for George to bring out his best game because he has a quick, young team-mate.

“Therefore it seemed pretty logical that Max would stay with Red Bull. Better the devil you know – that's a punchline! – and then wait what happens in two or three years, where contracts open up again and probably his options are not just one team but maybe three or four at a time. And wait who performs the best.”

Asked by Autosport if Mercedes had had any chance at all of hiring Verstappen for 2027, Wolff explained: “Pretty early in the late spring it was clear that we would continue like we do. And we have an open and in a way most transparent relationship as we can have. So the situation, as you say, was very different to what it was last year, where both sides were exploring whether cooperation could happen or not.”

The announcement of Verstappen’s new contract ended speculation over the four-time world champion’s future, after he emerged among drivers as arguably the most critical of F1’s new regulations. Cryptic, throwaway lines about “life” decisions to make fuelled rumours amid his involvement in GT3 racing, but in the end, Red Bull’s superstar decided to keep his F1 career going.

Asked if he was surprised to see Verstappen staying longer in the series, Wolff said: “No. The more regulations mature the more the teams will catch up. And even if Red Bull at the moment is on the back foot it is clear that, give it some time, they will shine.

“They have had strong races this year, others that were not. But I have no doubt that going forward the usual suspects will be again fighting for wins and championships, whether it is Ferrari or McLaren or Red Bull or ourselves. So the decision’s in a way logical one for me.”

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Norris pips Russell to grab pole
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has pipped George Russell to pole position for the Dutch Grand Prix with Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli rounding out the top three.

The reigning world champion beat sprint winner Russell by 0.102s to cap off a strong qualifying for McLaren, as the defending champions had topped every session at Zandvoort.

It came after Norris, who also topped Q2, had already claimed provisional pole with a 1m11.344s and that was 0.151s quicker than Russell with Oscar Piastri two tenths off in third.

Until then the session had been held in dry conditions but rain was about to fall down on the seaside track, causing a flurry of cars to soon leave the pitlane for their second laps in Q3.

This did cause some trouble though, as Norris and Russell entered the track at the same time and were seen racing each other on their out-laps with five minutes remaining.

Norris was first to cross the line, improving to a 1m11.163s on his final tour, and although Russell also bettered his time, it was only to a 1m11.265s.

They displaced Antonelli who had briefly gone to the top of the timesheet and Russell’s Mercedes team-mate was eventually 0.133s off pole with Piastri taking fourth.

George Russell, Mercedes Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

The Australian was 0.142s behind team-mate Norris and it will be an all-Ferrari third row with Lewis Hamilton in fifth, 0.331s off the pace, and Charles Leclerc sixth, 0.395s behind pole.

Seventh went to Red Bull’s home hero Max Verstappen, who was 0.455s behind Norris, and he will share the fourth row with temporary team-mate Liam Lawson as he is replacing the injured Isack Hadjar.

Gabriel Bortoleto qualified ninth for Audi and impressive Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad rounded out the top 10 on the day he achieved his fifth, straight Q3 appearance.

Pierre Gasly was just a tenth away from Q3 as he took 11th for Alpine and will share the sixth row with former team-mate and Racing Bulls stand-in Yuki Tsunoda upon his F1 return.

A late improvement from Nico Hulkenberg left the Audi veteran in 13th, meaning Gasly’s team-mate Franco Colapinto dropped to 14th ahead of Haas driver Esteban Ocon in 15th.

Zandvoort marks the first time since Miami-Imola-Monaco in May last year that the under pressure Ocon has outqualified team-mate Oliver Bearman on consecutive occasions.

Rounding out the Q2 drop zone was Alex Albon, whose team-mate Carlos Sainz suffered a second, consecutive Q1 exit as he took 17th on the weekend he’s signed a Williams contract extension.

Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing Photo by: Alastair Staley / LAT Images via Getty Images

Relatively speaking it was more positive for Aston Martin, who confirmed the step forward it has made with its upgraded engine and chassis despite drivability woes in the sprint sessions.

Fernando Alonso took 18th with team-mate Lance Stroll in 19th, while Bearman’s fears that Haas had regressed to becoming the ‘second-worst team’ came true as he qualified 20th.

That was ahead of only newcomer Cadillac, which was a second off making it into Q2 and 1.7s behind Piastri’s Q1 benchmark, with Valtteri Bottas taking 21st and Sergio Perez sitting in 22nd.

Sports.title: F1 Dutch GP: Russell controls sprint race as Leclerc overhauls Norris for second
Sports.content:
George Russell dominated the Dutch Grand Prix sprint race from pole for his third Saturday victory of the 2026 Formula 1 campaign.

The Mercedes driver led all the way from lights out in a rather processional affair, with Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and McLaren’s Lando Norris completing the podium at a dry Zandvoort.

It came after Russell grabbed pole on Friday after profiting from floor damage for his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who lost “25 points” of downforce due to an off at the penultimate corner in SQ1.

That left the championship leader fifth on the grid behind a front row of Russell and Norris, with Leclerc and Norris’ team-mate Oscar Piastri respectively lining up third and fourth.

At lights out Russell enjoyed a solid getaway by holding Norris at bay, but Antonelli immediately gained a place with a sweeping move around the outside of Piastri at Turn 1.

The 19-year-old applied instant pressure on Leclerc, who started on soft tyres compared to the rest on medium rubber, but as expected overtaking proved difficult.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

So the opening laps were rather static around the tight seaside circuit, but the evenly-matched drivers still remained within touching distance of each other as they preserved their tyres.

Everything started to ramp up though come lap 10 when Mercedes allowed Russell to push harder and the leader quickly streaked clear of a now vulnerable Norris by two seconds.

“I’ve got no rear,” reported the reigning world champion, who couldn’t keep his eyes off the Ferrari and Mercedes in his mirrors and that pressure from behind never died.

It resulted in Leclerc finally making his overtake down the inside of Norris at Turn 1 on lap 18 and while the Ferrari quickly pulled ahead, the McLaren still had to defend from Antonelli.

But once again at Zandvoort, staying within a second of the car in front is one thing, yet overtaking is another and all Norris really needed to do was keep it within the white lines.

That he did so the 26-year-old managed to hold on to third behind winner Russell, who crossed the line 1.4 seconds ahead of Leclerc, the Ferrari driver taking his third sprint podium of 2026.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Simon Galloway / LAT Images via Getty Images

Antonelli took fourth, 0.4s off Norris, with an extra 4.6s to fifth-placed Piastri who had Red Bull’s Max Verstappen just 0.3s behind in sixth in front of his home crowd.

Lewis Hamilton was never in contention aboard the sister Ferrari as he took seventh, with Alpine’s Pierre Gasly completing the points positions in eighth.

Sports.title: Norris passes Antonelli for second win in a row at Zandvoort | 2026 Dutch Grand Prix report
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed his second victory in a row in a lively Dutch Grand Prix.

The race was red-flagged at the end of the first lap after Max Verstappen crashed heavily at the final corner. The Red Bull driver was unhurt after spinning on the damp track and making heavy contact with the barrier.

Norris kept his lead from pole position at the original start while George Russell, who started alongside him, dropped back. But at the second standing start Andrea Kimi Antonelli made a much better getaway from second on the grid and passed his McLaren rival.

However Norris had good pace on the hard tyres and kept in touch with Antonelli. He delayed his second pit stop until six laps after his rival and quickly caught him in their third stint.

Lewis Hamilton delayed his second pit stop and took the lead of the race, and by lap 53 he had Antonelli and Norris in his mirrors. As Antonelli moved to pass him on the inside of Tarzan, Norris pounced and went around the outside of the Mercedes driver. Further around the lap, Hamilton appeared to have run out of energy, and Norris easily passed him on the run to the Hans Ernst Bocht.

Antonelli picked Hamilton off the next time by. However moments later Esteban Ocon’s Haas came to a stop, triggering a Virtual Safety Car period which changed the complexion of the final laps.

Hamilton dived into the pits, but as the VSC period dragged on Antonelli did likewise on the next lap. The race therefore restart with Norris leading Russell, both on old hard tyres, with Antonelli and Hamilton chasing after them on softs.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris’s pace on his hard rubber was excellent and he drew 10 seconds clear of Russell with 10 laps to go. Antonelli cruised up behind Russell, who immediately let his team mate through after Mercedes ordered him to.

A few laps later, Hamilton lined up Russell for an attack on the straight, but had to abandon his attack when another VSC period was triggered. This time the cause was debris left by a collision between the Williams drivers at Tarzan, Carlos Sainz Jnr having locked up and skidded into Alexander Albon.

Hamilton closed back up on Russell after the restart, but ran out of laps to pass his rival for third. Leclerc gained on the pair of them and closed suddenly on Hamilton as they approached Scheivlak on the final lap, clipping the rear of his team mate’s car.

Norris took the chequered flag 11 seconds ahead of Antonelli, while Russell claimed the final podium position. Oscar Piastri took sixth behind the Ferrari drivers.

Liam Lawson claimed seventh on his return to Red Bull despite receiving a 10-second time penalty for a yellow flag infringement. Nico Hulkenberg, who impressively avoided his spinning team mate on lap one, was rewarded with eighth place.

Fernando Alonso gave Aston Martin their best result of the season with ninth place in his updated car, followed by Pierre Gasly. Yuki Tsunoda missed out on a points finish on his return in 11th ahead of team mate Arvid Lindblad.

Sports.title: Dutch Grand Prix red-flagged after one lap due to huge crash for Verstappen | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Dutch Grand Prix has been red-flagged after a single lap due to a heavy crash for Max Verstappen.

The Red Bull driver spun into the barrier at the banked final corner at the end of the first lap.

The race began on a damp track, though Verstappen and all the other drivers opted for slick tyres. The final corner remained particularly wet.

Verstappen was in seventh place as the field reached the final corner. He appeared to touch the damp kerb on the inside of the corner, which tipped his car into a spin. As Verstappen attempted to correct the spin his car snapped hard to the left and made heavy contact with the barrier on the outside.

The Red Bull came to a rest shortly afterwards and Verstappen apologised to his team before climbing out.

Speaking after the race, Verstappen said the impact was not as serious as it could have been. “I think I still hit the SAFER barrier, maybe, potentially,” he said. “But I think also more frontal impact is actually a bit better than a sideways one, so from that sense, all okay.”

He wasn’t the only driver to lose control of his car in the damp final corner. The two Audi drivers almost collided after Gabriel Bortoleto spun in front of Nico Hulkenberg. While Bortoleto impressively regained control of his car without hitting the barrier, Hulkenberg performed a minor miracle in swerving to avoid his team mate. Both continued.

The race restarted at 3:33pm local time.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: A processional sprint race at Zandvoort | Brief
Sports.content:
Zandvoort’a first sprint race is also likely to be its last as the track does not have a contract to hold another round of the world championship. The race was a processional affair, which reader @Sham says showed the format’s shortcomings:

When a grand prix is processional, you can very often get a little tension from the slow build, from the strategy, from the way different cars and drivers use their tyres, from the way the track evolves, and all of the things that make Grand Prix racing great, and has done for decades.

With the sprint, you get nothing. At all. Nada.

The teams don’t even hide the fact that they use it as a practice session to fine tune the car any more.

Two out of 10 from me, only not a one because Leclerc chose soft tyres.

Sports.title: Small change made “unbelievable” improvement in Hamilton’s Ferrari | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton is optimistic about his chances in the Dutch Grand Prix after making a significant improvement in his Ferrari’s balance in qualifying.

He said he was surprised how much better his car felt on his way to fifth on the grid in qualifying after finishing seventh in the sprint race earlier today.

“I’m so much happier with the car,” said Hamilton. “Honestly, it’s crazy. We changed a lot of things, it doesn’t really look that big, but the difference it makes in the car is unbelievable.”

Hamilton said he felt happy with the car at the beginning of the weekend before qualifying for the sprint race.

“The difficult thing is I started P1 with good confidence, I lost it all in [sprint race] qualifying and all through the race I had no confidence in the balance. It was constantly breaking away from me.

“Then I go into [grand prix] qualifying and the car’s there, so the balance is there at least. So I was building and building and building. [If we had] some more laps I think we could have probably done better but I think ultimately the tyres were the issue for us.”

The Ferrari driver said he feels “a lot more optimistic for tomorrow with the balance that I have.”

However his team mate Charles Leclerc, who finished second in the sprint race, was less happy after taking sixth on the grid for the grand prix.

“We’ll have to look at two things, really,” he said. “The first one is mostly the fact that we started changing engine modes from Q1 to Q2 to Q3. Then the car is just doing different things underneath me, which is not something I enjoy, and we’ve probably missed a bit of performance there.

“Second is the prep[aration] lap that we have done that the others seem to not have done. I don’t feel like my tyres would have been ready without that preparation lap, but we’ve got to be open-minded and look at what the others have done.”

Sports.title: Rolly Romero Demands Teofimo Lopez Rematch
Sports.content:
Romero’s argument rests largely on who landed the punches that did the most damage.

He produced the fight’s clearest breakthrough in round five. Romero cut Lopez over the right eye, then hurt him with a left hook and looping right before pressing forward looking for the finish.

Lopez weathered it. Romero never found the final punch.

That distinction ultimately proved costly.

Romero disputed the scoring immediately afterward and dismissed the idea that Lopez had seriously troubled him.

“I got hit with two punches the whole fight that barely grazed me. I was never in any trouble. When I heard 114-114 I knew it was a robbery.”

The numbers tell another part of the fight.

CompuBox credited Lopez with a 124-73 advantage in total punches landed. His jab supplied much of that difference, connecting 62 times for a career high while Romero failed to land double-digit punches in every round except the fifth.

Lopez’s feet also forced Romero to continually rebuild his position before punching. Once Lopez recovered from the fifth, he spent longer stretches dictating the distance rather than exchanging where Romero carried the greater threat.

Romero still found him again.

A left hook late in the 11th knocked Lopez off balance and gave Romero another strong moment entering the championship round. He could not produce enough consistent work around those breakthroughs to convince two judges.

Lopez described his approach in simpler terms afterward.

“I just had to stay busy and keep my range against a strong puncher. I’m just looking forward to the next thing.”

That is the argument Romero now has to live with. He landed some of the night’s most damaging punches, while Lopez banked rounds with the jab, movement and higher output.

Romero had the openings to take the verdict out of the judges’ hands. He hurt Lopez in the fifth and caught him again in the 11th, but neither attack became a finish. Against a fighter banking rounds behind 62 landed jabs, isolated power shots leave too much arithmetic for three judges.

Sports.title: Hearn Says Anthony Joshua Contract Has Already Been Breached
Sports.content:
“What they want to do is they want to pay Anthony Joshua less money because that’s how it will work out with the difference in location. They want him to do a load of additional stuff. I’m not going to blow things up, which I could do so easily, but there has been breaches in AJ’s contract already which we’ve let slide because these guys are our partners and our friends, or were,” said Hearn.

Correcting “are” to “were” when describing the organizers as friends shows how badly the relationship has deteriorated. Hearn’s position is that Joshua signed for a British event and cannot be blamed for refusing to accept less money and additional duties merely because the preferred location changed.

Much of his anger was directed at a leaked Matchroom email containing a list of unresolved issues. Hearn believes it was deliberately circulated to journalists and falsely presented as Joshua’s demands for agreeing to fight in America.

None of the items in that email were included in the addendum Matchroom submitted for the proposed US move, he said. In Hearn’s view, the leak was intended to support Fury’s accusation that Joshua and Matchroom were being greedy and holding up the fight.

There were also claims that some people were financially encouraged to repost Fury’s version of events. Hearn offered no evidence during the press conference, so that allegation remains entirely his account. Still, anyone reading an alleged list of new demands without knowing it came from a separate email would naturally conclude that Joshua was asking for more.

The dispute extends to Dana White. Hearn says the agreement excludes TKO and Zuffa from promoting the event, despite White publicly identifying himself as its promoter. Nick Khan contacted Hearn about finding a way for TKO to participate, but White’s public approach had damaged those talks.

Time is nearly gone. The coming week was described as the deadline for preserving the proposed November date. Netflix needs time to promote the event, while Madison Square Garden may release the date and book something else. Joshua remains committed to fighting Fury, but the argument over location, money, and promotional control must be resolved within days.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Wants Three Unifications Without Facing One Mandatory
Sports.content:
During his post-fight press conference, Lopez said:

“I got three fights with DAZN, and all of them are the road to undisputed. We’re going right to every world title. We’re not taking no title defense, no nothing. Whoever’s next, we’re going for him.”

A unification technically includes a defense of the belts involved, but Lopez’s meaning was clear. He does not plan to face an ordinary mandatory or ranked challenger between attempts to collect the other titles. If that plan proceeds, it will consume well over a year. Each fight requires negotiations between promoters, networks and boxing organizations before the participants complete training camps and recover afterward. Lopez also left the Romero fight with a cut over his right eyebrow that may delay his return.

The first unification depends on another event. Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are scheduled to fight on September 12, after which the winner will need time to recover and negotiate with Lopez. The next stage against Liam Paro or Devin Haney requires another lengthy round of discussions.

Completing all three fights may leave contenders in several organizations waiting 12 to 18 months. Some will be forced into additional bouts to protect their rankings while the champion moves from one financially attractive unification to another.

Unifications often receive priority because reducing the number of champions is supposed to benefit boxing. That principle becomes difficult to defend when it is used repeatedly to prevent every other challenger from receiving an opportunity.

Granting one exception for a major fight is understandable. Three consecutive exceptions create a separate set of rules for the boxer who generates the most money. Ranked contenders must keep winning while Teofimo remains protected from facing any of them.

The strategy also depends on Lopez winning every fight. A loss transfers the collected titles to another champion, who may then request additional exceptions for more lucrative bouts. The waiting challengers must begin the same process again with someone new.

The schedule Teofimo described requires approval from more than DAZN. The WBA and the other organizations must authorize each step. If they permit three straight unifications without requiring a mandatory defense, the “road to undisputed” will become another example of boxing’s business interests overriding its competitive structure.

Sports.title: Catterall Threatens Teofimo Lopez’s Big-Money Welterweight Plans
Sports.content:
A majority decision over Rolando Romero at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas gave Lopez the belt. His steady pressure, jab and body work earned scores of 116-112 and 115-113, while the third judge returned a 114-114 card.

Watching from outside the ring, Catterall made his opinion clear on social media.

“I beat either of these pair no doubt in my mind,” said Catterall on X about Teofimo and Rolly.

That confidence is not difficult to understand after Lopez’s welterweight debut. Romero spent long stretches moving backward and waiting for one power counter. His low output allowed Lopez to win rounds through activity without producing a dominant offensive performance.

When Romero finally attacked in the fifth, he hurt Teofimo with a left hand and opened a cut over his right eyebrow. Lopez recovered and regained control, but he never seriously hurt Romero despite landing the cleaner punches for much of the fight.

A more difficult test comes from Catterall. The British southpaw will not concede as many quiet rounds. His timing, counters and disciplined defense can disrupt Teofimo’s lead hand and force him to reset before attacking. He also has the patience to punish the wide punches Teofimo throws when he becomes frustrated.

The WBA ordered its Super champion to face the winner of Jack Catterall vs. Shakhram Giyasov within 180 days of their May 23 bout. Catterall won that fight and holds the secondary WBA welterweight title, placing him next in line for a consolidation bout. The period ends on November 19, although the WBA has not issued a new public order naming Lopez since he defeated Romero. The original WBA ruling established the timetable.

The cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow may delay the consolidation fight. November 19 is less than three months away, leaving limited time for the wound to heal before he resumes sparring and completes another camp. His team can request a medical extension if contact training places the cut at risk of reopening. Any added time would only postpone the obligation unless Catterall accepts a step-aside agreement or the WBA grants Lopez permission to take another fight. That delay may allow Lopez’s team to pursue Garcia, Benn or Haney.

Less money and greater risk make Catterall an opponent Teofimo has little reason to welcome. Based on Saturday’s performance, Lopez will need more than steady pressure and a busy jab against a disciplined southpaw who will make him pay for every mistake.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Defeats Rolly Romero, Captures WBA Title
Sports.content:
That was Romero’s best stretch of the fight. Lopez recovered in the sixth and resumed moving forward behind his jab while attacking the body. Although the cut began bleeding again late in the contest, he continued outworking a champion who spent too much time waiting for isolated counterpunching opportunities.

Needing a strong finish, Romero remained cautious during the 12th. Lopez stayed on the front foot and completed the fight as the busier boxer. The victory raised his record to 23-2 with 13 knockouts, while Romero dropped to 17-3 with 13 stoppages.

Gary Antonio Russell Takes Santillan’s Interim Belt

A dominant unanimous decision over Victor Santillan gave Gary Antonio Russell the interim WBA super bantamweight title. Scores were 119-108 twice and 118-109.

Superior speed, a sharp jab and faster combinations allowed Russell to control the fight. The matchup between two southpaws produced frequent clinches, but Russell consistently landed the cleaner punches whenever space opened between them.

A right hook to the top of the head dropped Santillan during the 12th round. He beat referee Robert Hoyle’s count and held repeatedly to survive until the final bell. Russell moved to 22-1 with 13 knockouts, while Santillan fell to 16-3 with seven stoppages.

Hernandez Receives Majority Decision Over Veron

A majority decision over Francisco Daniel Veron gave Yoenli “El Diablo” Hernandez the victory in their 10-round middleweight bout. Two judges scored it widely for Hernandez at 99-91 and 98-92, while the third returned a surprising 95-95 card.

Heavier and more accurate punches gave Hernandez control during the opening rounds, while Veron tried to compensate with pressure and a high work rate. Veron created his best moment in the fifth when a check hook briefly wobbled Hernandez and forced him toward the ropes.

The Cuban regained control by attacking the body and landing right hands and uppercuts. Veron continued advancing and throwing through the final bell, but many of his punches missed or struck Hernandez’s guard.

Utria Edges Mercado By Split Decision

A disputed split decision over Israel “Bad Ways” Mercado kept Carlos Utria’s perfect record intact after their 10-round light welterweight fight. Scores were 96-94 for Utria, 96-94 for Mercado and 97-93 for Utria.

Much of the early action belonged to Utria before Mercado closed the fourth with a combination. The fight remained close through the middle rounds, with neither boxer establishing a lasting advantage.

Strong work during the ninth carried Mercado into a decisive final round. He believed he had done enough to win, and sections of the crowd expressed their displeasure when Utria was announced as the victor.

Marco Romero Stops Kahlil Mitchell In First

A sustained attack from Marco Romero forced a first-round stoppage against Kahlil “Killa” Mitchell in their scheduled eight-round bout.

Unable to defend himself, Mitchell was trapped as Romero unloaded a combination during the final minute. Referee Allen Huggins stopped the contest at 2:33.

Johnson Decisions Rodriguez

A six-round decision over Jose Gabriel Rodriguez gave Benjamin Johnson another welterweight victory. Johnson moved to 8-0 with seven knockouts, while Rodriguez dropped to 4-4-1.

Tony Weeks served as the referee.

Brown Sweeps Wiggins Over Six Rounds

Every round went to Joseph “The Prodigy” Brown in a slow six-round middleweight contest against Alton Wiggins. All three judges scored the fight 60-54.

Cleaner punches separated Brown from Wiggins, whose frequent holding prevented the exchanges from developing. The same pattern continued through the sixth.

Blancas Drops Mamone, Wins Decision

A knockdown helped Aldo Blancas secure a unanimous decision over Ricky Mamone in their four-round light welterweight bout. Scores were 39-36 twice and 40-35.

A left hook to the body from Blancas produced a delayed knockdown late in the second. Mamone beat referee John McCarthy’s count and continued despite bleeding from the nose during the third.

Unable to secure the stoppage, Blancas settled for the decision after Mamone survived the final round.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Wins Third Belt As Rolando Romero Barely Fights
Sports.content:
Romero’s strategy depended almost entirely on catching Lopez as he moved inside. That opportunity arrived in the fifth round when a left hand opened a cut over Lopez’s right eyebrow and hurt him. Romero followed with a flurry and had the challenger under pressure as “Rolly” chants spread through the arena.

It should have changed the fight. Instead, Romero returned to waiting.

Lopez recovered in the sixth, reestablished his jab and resumed attacking the body. Blood continued leaking from the cut during the later rounds, but it never prevented him from moving forward or maintaining his output. Romero landed isolated counters without putting enough punches behind them to take control.

The champion’s corner urged him to hold the center of the ring before the final round. He continued moving away and never produced the desperate attack required from a fighter in danger of losing his belt. By then, the crowd had grown restless after repeatedly waiting for Romero to open up.

Lopez deserves credit for remaining disciplined after being hurt. He avoided turning the fight into the reckless exchange Romero needed, kept scoring with straightforward work and closed the championship rounds on the front foot. The performance was controlled rather than destructive, with Lopez winning through activity, positioning and better decision-making.

His welterweight debut also raised a question about his punching power at 147 pounds. Lopez landed plenty of clean shots but never seriously hurt Romero. That may become important against the stronger and more active fighters in the division.

Still, Lopez accomplished what he came to Las Vegas to do. He won a title in a third weight class, while Romero surrendered his belt through passivity after finding the punch that briefly gave him a chance to take over the fight.

Sports.title: Yoenli Hernandez Beats Franciso Veron, But Draw Card Stuns
Sports.content:
Early confidence led the Cuban to lower his hands, pose and attack with wide power shots. He controlled the distance when he used his jab and footwork, then punished Veron with right hands, uppercuts and combinations to the body whenever the Argentine moved inside.

Veron’s persistence created one dangerous moment. A check hook late in the fifth round caught Hernandez cleanly, briefly wobbling him and forcing him toward the ropes. It was the clearest round for Veron and a reminder that Hernandez was taking unnecessary chances against an opponent who refused to retreat.

The favorite responded by tightening his defense and resuming his body attack. Hernandez hurt Veron with a right hand early in the eighth, followed with uppercuts and continued landing the stronger punches through the championship rounds. Veron absorbed the punishment and kept throwing, but his aggression rarely produced clean scoring shots.

That inability to secure the stoppage will give Hernandez something to study. He had the size, power and technical advantage, yet spent too much time looking for single explosive punches instead of breaking Veron down with sustained combinations. His performance was convincing without being the destructive statement his team likely wanted.

None of that explains the draw score. Hernandez clearly won more than five rounds, and the 95-95 card turned an otherwise straightforward result into an unnecessary controversy. The two wide scores properly reflected a fight controlled by Hernandez, even if Veron’s toughness forced him to work until the final bell.

Sports.title: Rolando Romero vs Teofimo Lopez Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Yoenli Hernandez Defeats Francisco Veron

Yoenli Hernandez powered past Francisco Daniel Veron by majority decision, earning 99-91 and 98-92 cards while a third judge scored it 95-95. Hernandez attacked the body and landed the cleaner, heavier punches, although Veron’s check hook badly shook him in the fifth. Hernandez recovered and took command again down the stretch.

Gary Antonio Russell seized the interim WBA super bantamweight title with a commanding unanimous decision over Victor Santillan. Russell’s faster hands, jab and combinations controlled the fight before he dropped Santillan in the 12th. The judges scored it 119-108 twice and 118-109.

Carlos Utria survived a demanding U.S. debut and defeated Israel Mercado by split decision. Mercado pressed and disrupted Utria’s rhythm, but Utria’s body attack and short combinations secured 97-93 and 96-94 cards, while Mercado took the third 96-94.

Ghana News.title: Duncan Amoah: Gov’t should create conditions for 24-hour economy, not build markets
Ghana News.content:
Executive Secretary of the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC), Duncan Amoah, has criticised the government’s approach to the implementation of the 24-hour economy, arguing that public funds should not be used primarily to construct markets under the initiative.

According to him, the government’s focus should instead be on creating the conditions that will encourage businesses and consumers to participate in economic activities at night.

“Government does not, for me, have a business going to build markets. I don’t subscribe to that one,” Mr Amoah said.

He argued that constructing physical infrastructure without addressing key barriers to night-time economic activity, including inadequate security and street lighting, could result in public funds being wasted.

“You can build an ultra-modern market in a village; if their culture and subculture is to sleep by 6 pm, that market will be there in ruins. You would have wasted all that money, all that effort,” he said.

Mr Amoah said government should instead create an environment in which businesses can operate beyond the traditional working day without exposing workers and customers to unnecessary risks.

“Create the environment such that if I could afford to get home at nine and I can do two more hours outside,” he said.

He noted that businesses such as salons, pharmacies and shops could benefit from increased economic activity at night if the necessary conditions were provided.

Call for stronger night-time security

Mr Amoah also called for improved security and street lighting, arguing that many Ghanaians remain reluctant to go out at night because of fears of robbery and other criminal activity.

He urged the police to increase their presence at night and called for better lighting in communities and along major roads.

“The number of men you put out there in the daytime, double it at night. We don’t want just the stop police checkpoints. We want to see them,” he said.

According to him, improved security would give people the confidence to park their vehicles, shop, eat out and engage in other economic activities after dark without fear.

Incentives to drive night-time activity

Mr Amoah further suggested the use of incentives to stimulate demand during off-peak hours, including encouraging businesses to offer selected goods and services at lower prices at night.

He said the 24-hour economy should therefore not be reduced to the construction of physical facilities, but supported by policies that make the additional 12 hours economically productive.

“The other 12-hour period is wasted because it’s dark,” Mr Amoah said.

He called on the government to rethink and reprogramme its approach to the 24-hour economy to deliver visible changes that would encourage more Ghanaians to participate in the night-time economy.

Ghana News.title: JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair finale turns homeownership dreams into real possibilities
Ghana News.content:
The JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair 2026 is close to ending at the Achimota Retail Centre, after three days of conversations, exhibitions and practical opportunities for people looking to build, buy, finance or improve their homes.

The final day of the mini-fair on Sunday, August 23, attracted patrons who moved from stand to stand, engaging exhibitors and exploring solutions across Ghana’s housing and construction sector.

Held under the theme “Dream it. Explore it. Own it,” the fair was designed to take homeownership beyond aspiration by putting prospective homeowners in direct contact with businesses and professionals who could help them take the next step.

From building materials and construction solutions to home financing, property development, furnishing and home improvement, exhibitors used the three-day event to showcase products and services while responding to questions from visitors.

For many patrons, the experience was as much about getting answers as it was about looking at products.

Visitors had the opportunity to compare options, speak directly with industry players, and better understand some of the decisions involved in building or owning a home.

The strong interest continued through the weekend despite intermittent rain in Accra on Saturday and Sunday, with patrons still making their way to the fairgrounds to engage exhibitors.

The fair brought together a range of companies and service providers across the housing value chain, including Akwaaba Building Materials, Lesh Fortune Ltd, MTN, Door Masters, Ayuda, Western Vilas, CTECHI Ghana LTD, Saint-Gobain Ghana, Sintex Tank, Interplast and Clifton Homes.

The initiative was organised in partnership with Republic Bank, under its brand promise “We’re the one for you!”, and powered by Drive EV GH.

As the exhibition comes to an end, the emphasis remains on helping prospective homeowners move from simply imagining the home they want to practical decisions about how to achieve it.

For some visitors, that could mean finding the right building materials. For others, it could mean understanding financing options, exploring property opportunities or identifying professionals who can help turn an idea into a plan.

That practical connection between the dream of owning a home and the steps required to achieve it has been at the heart of the 2026 Habitat Fair.

The conversations started at the fair are expected to continue in homes, offices, construction sites and financial institutions, where many of the decisions about Ghana’s next generation of homes will ultimately be made.

Ghana News.title: Bamiri chief commissions KG block, guest house to boost education and revenue
Ghana News.content:
The Chief of Bamiri and Tuntuhene of the Techiman Traditional Council, Nana Asare Baffour II, has commissioned two major development projects in the community as part of this year’s Yam Festival celebrations.

The projects, comprising a modern Kindergarten (KG) block and a guest house, are intended to improve the safety and learning environment for children while generating revenue to support the community’s development needs.

The commissioning ceremonies were attended by traditional leaders, community members and school authorities.

New KG block to improve safety and learning environment

The new KG facility was constructed partly in response to concerns over the safety of children at the old school premises, where pupils were exposed to traffic risks while playing or crossing nearby roads.

Nana Asare Baffour II said the safety of children was a major motivation for providing the new facility.

“I could not sit back and watch our children risk their lives every day just to get an education,” he said.

“This Kindergarten block is my contribution to their safety and to the improvement of education in Bamiri. Every child deserves a secure environment to learn and grow.”

The Headmistress of the school, Gifty Adjei Sarpong, who received the facility on behalf of the school, expressed appreciation to the chief for the intervention.

She said the project had come at a critical time and had addressed the school’s longstanding accommodation challenges.

“This facility has come at the right time. It has solved our accommodation problems and given our children a safe space to learn,” she said.

Madam Sarpong, however, appealed for additional support for teaching and learning materials to enable the school to make full use of the new facility.

Guest house to generate funds for development

The chief also commissioned a newly constructed guest house, which is expected to generate revenue for the community.

Located within the Techiman township, the facility is intended to accommodate visitors, travellers and business people who patronise the area.

Proceeds from the guest house will be channelled into community development projects to reduce Bamiri’s reliance on external support.

Nana Asare Baffour II said the facility formed part of a broader strategy to make the community more financially self-sufficient.

“We cannot depend on handouts forever,” he said.

“This Guest House will generate revenue for the community, which will in turn support other developmental initiatives. It is about building a sustainable future for Bamiri.”

Bamiri’s development

Bamiri has in recent years developed from a predominantly farming community into a growing township with a population of more than 5,000.

The community now has several basic social and economic amenities, including a water supply system, police station, CHPS compound, fabrication company, technical institute, public place of convenience and a gari processing factory.

The addition of the KG block and guest house is expected to further strengthen the community’s infrastructure and support its development ambitions.

The projects were commissioned as part of this year’s Yam Festival, which attracted hundreds of residents and visitors to Bamiri.

Ghana News.title: Data Protection Commission acquires two vehicles to strengthen data protection enforcement
Ghana News.content:
The Data Protection Commission (DPC) has acquired two new pickup vehicles to strengthen its enforcement operations and expand its activities across the country.

The vehicles, purchased with the Commission’s Internally Generated Funds (IGF), will support field operations and the planned establishment of regional offices to improve compliance with Ghana’s data protection laws.

Deputy Minister of Communications, Digital Technology and Innovations, Mohammed Adams Sukparu, presented the vehicles to the Commission at a ceremony in Accra on Thursday.

Speaking to the Ghana News Agency after the presentation, Executive Director of the DPC, Dr Arnold Kavaarpuo, said the Commission had designated 2026 as the “Year of Enforcement” to ensure that institutions comply with their obligations under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843).

He explained that public and private institutions that process or intend to process personal information are required to register with the Commission.

Dr Kavaarpuo, however, stressed that compliance goes beyond registration, with institutions expected to establish appropriate policies and safeguards to protect personal information.

These include conducting vulnerability and penetration assessments where necessary, as well as data protection impact assessments for significant data-processing activities.

He said the Commission would pay particular attention to sensitive information, including children’s data, health records and information with potential national security implications.

Dr Kavaarpuo also cautioned educational institutions against using images of children for promotional purposes without obtaining the necessary consent.

“Those students are there to school. They are not marketing objects,” he said.

On health data, he said the DPC would intensify scrutiny of how institutions collect, store, access and share such information because of its sensitive nature.

According to him, the Commission initially faced challenges with its enforcement drive because limited public awareness meant some institutions only became aware of the regulator after enforcement action had commenced.

He said the DPC had therefore incorporated public education into its enforcement activities to deepen understanding of the law and encourage voluntary compliance.

The Commission also expects its planned regional expansion to improve access to its services, particularly for individuals seeking redress following data breaches or the misuse of their personal information.

Dr Kavaarpuo stressed that data protection should also be treated as a national security concern, given the risks posed by identity theft, unauthorised access and other threats to Ghana’s data infrastructure.

“Data is as much a national security imperative as it is a commercial or personal nature,” he said.

The Data Protection Commission was established under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843), in line with the constitutional right to privacy.

It is responsible for regulating the processing of personal information, promoting compliance with data protection requirements and protecting individuals against the misuse of their personal data.

Ghana News.title: NSMQ 2026: Holy Child School storms back from two-year NSMQ absence to book One-Eighth ticket
Ghana News.content:
Holy Child School has announced its return to the NSMQ National Championship in emphatic fashion, surviving a fierce preliminary-stage battle against Anlo SHS and Nkawkaw SHS to secure a ticket to the One-Eighth Stage.

After a two-year absence from the National Championship, Holy Child School wasted no time reminding the competition of its pedigree, dominating the contest at the SMS Auditorium and finishing on 67 points.

But the victory was far from a walk in the park. The Stars of Anlo Land pushed Holy Child School all the way, finishing strongly on 52 points, while Nkawkaw SHS ended the contest on 35 points.

The opening round immediately set the tone for a tense afternoon, with just a single point separating Holy Child School and Anlo SHS.

Holy Child School opened with 25 points, Anlo SHS followed closely with 24, while Nkawkaw SHS stayed within striking distance on 21.

Then came the Speed Race — and the pressure intensified. The first four questions went unanswered, with Anlo SHS making attempts but failing to convert them. When the fifth question finally fell, Holy Child School seized the opportunity and gradually took control of the round.

By the end of Round Two, Holy Child School had stretched its lead to 35 points, with Anlo SHS on 26 and Nkawkaw SHS on 20.

A Perfect Showdown

The Problem of the Day produced one of the biggest moments of the contest. Both Holy Child School and Anlo SHS delivered perfect 10/10 scores, earning the two schools the coveted NSMQ Star Award.

Holy Child School carried that momentum into the next round, moving to 45 points, while Anlo SHS reached 36 and Nkawkaw SHS 25.

But Anlo SHS was not done. In the True or False Round, the Stars of Anlo Land produced a flawless performance, answering every question correctly.

The perfect run earned Anlo SHS the Clean Sheet Award, injecting fresh excitement into the contest.

Holy Child School, however, refused to surrender its advantage.

The comeback challenge from Anlo SHS was met with another composed performance from Holy Child School, which ended the round on 58 points.

Anlo SHS stood at 52, while Nkawkaw SHS had 32. With the contest heading into the final Riddle Round, the battle for supremacy was still alive.

Holy Child School then delivered the final blow. The school cracked three riddles, securing the GOIL Riddle Bonanza and putting the contest beyond doubt.

When the final scores flashed on the scoreboard, the two-year wait was officially over.

HOLY CHILD SCHOOL — 67

ANLO SHS — 52

NKAWKAW SHS — 35

Holy Child School's triumphant return earns it a place in the One-Eighth Stage of the NSMQ 2026 National Championship, while Anlo SHS's spirited challenge produced two major individual honours, the NSMQ Star Award and Clean Sheet Award.

For Holy Child School, it was more than just a preliminary-stage victory. After two years away, the comeback could hardly have been louder.

The GNFS also reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and an open-door policy in communicating with personnel and the public, while urging everyone to disregard the report and refrain from circulating what it described as misinformation.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
