World.title: Prime minister in Kyiv: Russia shouldn't count on us tiring of Ukraine support
World.content:
Ukraine must receive everything it needs to defend itself, Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) said as he arrived in Kyiv for an NB8 summit with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Michal is in the Ukrainian capital on Sunday and will co-chair a summit of Nordic-Baltic (NB8) and Ukrainian leaders with Zelenskyy, and will take part in events marking Ukraine's National Flag Day.

Estonia holds the NB8 presidency this year, and Michal's visit comes at a time of intensified attacks by Russia on Kyiv and Ukraine and stalled diplomatic efforts.

The visit also closely follows the 35th anniversary of the restoration of Estonian independence. "This year marks 35 years since Estonia restored its independence and Ukraine declared its independence. Both our countries secured the right to decide their own future. Today, Ukraine is defending that right on the battlefield while standing up for the freedom and security of all Europe," Michal said.

The Nordic and Baltic countries have stood with Ukraine since the first day of Russia's full-scale war of aggression, now in its fifth year. "Ukraine must receive everything it needs to defend itself and resist Russian aggression," the prime minister went on, via a press release.

He noted that "everything Ukraine needs" primarily means more air defense, more ammunition and greater investment in Ukraine's defense industry. "At the same time, we must increase pressure on Russia, strengthen sanctions and close the loopholes Russia uses to evade them," Michal added.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal is in Kyiv Sunday for national flag day and to co-chair the NB8-Ukraine meeting, along with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Source: Government Office

"We are helping Ukraine prepare for winter and protect and restore critical energy infrastructure, which remains under threat because of Russia's brutality," the head of government went on.

While in Kyiv, Michal will meet his Ukrainian counterpart, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, to discuss bilateral relations and preparations for the Ukraine Recovery Conference to be held in Tallinn in January next year.

Michal's visit also coincides with Ukraine's National Flag Day, which is marked annually on August 23.

The NB8 format brings together the Nordic countries — Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden — and the Baltic states — Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania — for regular dialogue on security and regional issues. Following the summit, a joint press conference is expected to outline outcomes and new commitments, as Estonia's NB8 presidency has placed regional security and support for Ukraine at the top of the agenda.

Estonia has been one of Ukraine's strongest supporters since the full-scale invasion began in February 2022, providing military aid, humanitarian assistance and political backing, while consistently calling for increased international pressure on Russia. The Reconstruction Conference in Tallinn next January will bring together international partners to coordinate Ukraine's long-term recovery, and Michal's visit continues a pattern of high-level engagement between the two countries.

Michal's visit is scheduled to last one day, with the prime minister returning to Estonia later Sunday.

The summit comes as diplomatic efforts to end the war remain stalled, with Russia insisting any deal must reflect "realities on the ground" — a reference to its control of around one-fifth of Ukrainian territory. On the battlefield, fighting has intensified, while Russia continues its long-range strikes on Ukrainian cities . Ukraine has expanded its own deep strikes inside Russia.

World.title: Minister: Russia's behavior unchanged since Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, 87 years on
World.content:
Russia's behavior has remained unchanged in the nine decades since the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact was signed, Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said.

Sunday, August 23, is Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact memorial day, marking 87 years since the Soviet Union and Nazi Germany signed the infamous deal. The pact's secret protocols carved Europe, including Estonia, into spheres of influence which paved the way for the occupation of sovereign states.

Tsahkna noted that the Soviet Union's successor state, the Russian Federation, has changed little since then. "Russia continues trying to redraw Europe's borders according to its imperial ambitions. Its refusal to accept the collapse of the Soviet Union and the fall of the communist Eastern Bloc is the root cause of today's war of aggression against Ukraine," he said. "Just as the Soviet Union ultimately failed to reshape Europe's balance of power under the MRP secret protocol, Russia's current attempt to restore its sphere of influence will fail as well," Tsahkna said via a press release.

He underscored the pact, which was built on lies and cynical geopolitics, set in motion nearly 50 years of Baltic occupation and the repression, deportation, and imprisonment of tens of thousands. "Although the Baltic Way (Baltic chain) exposed the secret protocol 37 years ago and helped us restore our independence, the consequences of those repressions still echo in almost every Estonian family," Tsahkna went on.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200). Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

"On MRP Memorial Day, we honor all those in Estonia and beyond who endured the brutal crimes of totalitarian and authoritarian regimes," he added, highlighting Ukraine's present-day struggles in fending off with exceptional skill and determination an invasion by a totalitarian regime. "The so-called 'special military operation' has become a costly five-year war. The front line has stalled, and in recent months Ukraine's deep strikes against Russia's critical infrastructure have generated significant strategic momentum."

"At the same time, international sanctions are having a tangible effect. Russia's economy is under strain, internal tensions are rising, and Putin has grown visibly more anxious. As long as Moscow refuses to abandon its goals, our task is to ensure that Russia's international isolation holds and support for Ukraine remains unwavering," Tsahkna added.

The minister stressed that aggression is most likely to recur when it is not met with consequences. "We must stand united to ensure that those who try to shatter peace by force and pursue their ambitions are held accountable. International crimes carry unavoidable responsibility."

The MRP was a "non-aggression" agreement signed by Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union on August 23, 1939, by the foreign ministers of both regimes, Vyacheslav Molotov and Joachim von Ribbentrop. The secret protocols which carved up Central and Eastern Europe under German and Soviet spheres of influence and paved the way for World War II saw Estonia, an independent nation for over 20 years by then, placed under the Soviet sphere. The 1989 Baltic Way protest, which saw a human chain stretch from Vilnius to Tallinn, highlighted the occupation of all three Baltic states resulting from the pact on its 50th anniversary.

World.title: French triathlete wins Tallinn Ironman, Estonian 10th in record field
World.content:
Kristofer Kamberg was the top Estonian competitor, finishing 10th.

The event went ahead despite the windy conditions and Level 2 storm warning, with Conte completing the course in a time of eight hours and eight minutes.

"It's now been three years since I last finished an Ironman. It's all emotional, but I'm very happy," Conte told ERR after the race.

The race is the largest triathlon in the Baltic states and attracted a record 4,300 entrants this year, for the full triathlon on Saturday and the 70.3 half-distance on Sunday. Around 1,500 people were involved in staffing the event, whose headquarters was the Unibet Arena.

Kristofer Kamberg. Source: ERR

Chief organizer Ain-Alar Juhanson told ERR a total of 97 nations are represented in the event across all categories, with 1,900 people due to start the full race, almost as many competing in the 70.3 race, as well as 150 teams. "Those are numbers we have never seen here before," Juhanson added.

Lake Raku, just south of Tallinn, was used for the swimming stage for the first time.

The toughest part of the 226-kilometer race for the winner turned out to be the final discipline, the run. "The start of the swim was delayed a little because of fog. We started later. The bike was okay, a bit of wind, and I didn't get any rain at first. But it started raining at the beginning of the second lap of the run," Conte noted.

Kamberg completed the course in eight hours and 37 minutes, 29 minutes behind the winner, giving him 10th place. "It wasn't easy. In fact, it was hard the whole time. The weather was probably in our favor, even though it's raining, because it didn't get hot, and my first reaction is: damn, this really is hard," Kamberg said.

Ironman 70.3 Tallinn swimming stage at last year's event. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

This was only his second Ironman, and he called himself a "below-average Estonian amateur" who had not put a massive emphasis on training in the run-up to the event. In a triathlon context, his level of modest training would take up about 10–12 hours a week. "I was actually a little worried about that coming here," he continued, and, as with Conte, found the run the hardest part.

"My leg muscles started giving out midway through the run, and that was really the main reason my pace dropped off as it did," Kamberg added.

The Baltics' largest triathlon festival culminates in Tallinn on Sunday with a half-distance race, where Estonians Kaidi Kivioja and Henry Räppo defend their titles. The event is already underway at the time of writing.

Kaidi Kivioja. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

In the women's race, Kivioja is looking to repeat last year's win, and her Estonian record over the full distance at the European Championships in Germany in June bodes well for that.

"You can't just look at past results and assume that anything is guaranteed this Sunday. But I'm going to go out there and give it my best," Kivioja said, noting she took on a new coach and new training regime this year.

Some of the traffic restrictions in place Saturday will remain in place on Sunday. The 70.3 race got underway at 9.00 a.m. today.

World.title: Baghdad hosts Iraqi-Libyan Joint Committee meetings after 25-year hiatus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Libya’s Acting Foreign Minister Taher al-Baour is in Baghdad heading a high-level delegation to co-chair the Iraqi-Libyan Joint Committee meetings, which have resumed after a 25-year break.

Al-Baour met with Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein to discuss strategies to enhance political, diplomatic, and regional ties between Baghdad and Tripoli.

Their discussions focused on aligning mutual political positions on regional problems and increasing combined consular and diplomatic presence.

Following their meeting, al-Baour and Hussein held a joint press conference. Al-Baour emphasized Libya’s immediate need to partner with Iraq to repair and staff key public facilities, particularly in education and healthcare.

The Libyan delegation is finalizing several memoranda of understanding covering a wide range of economic and development areas.

Al-Baour’s team includes officials from several government bodies affiliated with the Tripoli-based Government of National Unity (GNU).

According to the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, this diplomatic drive follows Iraq’s offer to resume coordination and signify a return to normalized, regular diplomatic ties between the two countries.

The delegation’s trip to Baghdad builds directly upon virtual expert meetings organized by the Libyan Ministry of Foreign Affairs to conclude trade agreements with Iraqi officials before signatures are authorized.

World.title: Japanese archaeological missions to return to Iraq for excavations and training
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Japanese archaeological excavation teams are preparing to return to Iraq to conduct scientific digs and provide hands-on field training for local researchers, according to statements made on Sunday, August 23, 2026, by Dr. Laith Majeed Hussein, Director of the Japanese–Iraqi Institute for Archaeological Education.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Hussein outlined that bilateral cooperation is expanding beyond field excavation to encompass academic faculty recruitment from Japan and Egypt to support the Department of Japanese Language and Literature at the University of Baghdad’s College of Arts.

Key Academic Initiatives & Archaeological Milestones

Resumption of Japanese Excavation Missions: Japanese archaeological teams—holding a multi-decade legacy of Mesopotamian field research—are coordinating their return following improvements in domestic security conditions to resume field surveying, artifact conservation, and joint research.

Hands-on Field Training: Upcoming excavation seasons will integrate joint fieldwork, pairing Japanese specialists and university students with Iraqi researchers and trainees to teach modern stratigraphic excavation and surveying methods.

Expansion of Japanese Language Studies: To build language proficiency and strengthen cultural exchange, the University of Baghdad’s College of Arts is recruiting native instructors and specialized faculty from Japan and Egypt to teach within its Japanese Language Department.

Institutional Heritage Ties: Dr. Hussein highlighted the historical roots of bilateral academic engagement, citing the establishment of the Center for the Revival of Arab Scientific Heritage in Baghdad in 1977, founded in close partnership with Japanese academic institutions.

International Assyriology Conference: Hussein noted that Baghdad had finalized preparations to host the 2026 Rencontre Assyriologique Internationale (International Congress of Assyriology); however, regional security tensions prompted a postponement, with organizers preparing to reapply for international convening approvals for a future date.

The revival of Japanese archaeological missions reflects the broader international reintegration of Iraq’s academic and heritage institutions.

By combining field excavations with university-level language instruction and peer-reviewed publishing partnerships, the Japanese–Iraqi Institute for Archaeological Education aims to equip a new generation of Iraqi scholars with advanced excavation methodologies and promote the preservation of Mesopotamian cultural heritage.

World.title: Economist: Iran Hormuz permits ‘too late’ as tankers secure safe passage
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi economic expert Ziyad Al-Hashemi stated on Saturday, August 22, 2026, that international crude buyers have successfully expanded oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz independently, making Tehran’s recent exceptional passage permits redundant.

According to Al-Hashemi’s analysis, published on social media and reported by regional news platforms, maritime tracking indicators show that commercial operators adapted to regional security risks days before official Iranian clearances were publicized. Consequently, he described Tehran’s formal approval as a late public-relations gesture aimed at courting the Iraqi public rather than a decisive logistical breakthrough.

Maritime Analytics & Key Operational Metrics

1 to 2 Million BPD Flowing: Energy market and maritime analytics from Vortexa confirm that seaborne crude volumes traversing the Strait of Hormuz averaged between 1 million and 2 million barrels per day (bpd) over the past 10 days, primarily originating from Iraq and Saudi Arabia.

Regional Total Reaching 3M BPD: Adding daily crude and fuel consignments from Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates, total maritime throughput across the waterway reached approximately 3 million bpd.

Adoption of “Dark Sailings”: Energy trading firms and shipping lines adapted by deploying smaller tankers and executing “dark sailings”—turning off or minimizing Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponders—to obscure vessel positions and reduce targeting risks during transit.

Declining Maritime Attacks: Despite an increase in passing tanker traffic, maritime incidents and Iranian interdictions declined notably over the same period, signaling either altered strategic calculations regarding the Strait of Hormuz or diminished operational capacity to sustain maritime disruption.

Diminished Strategic Value of Permits: Because international buyers and shipping syndicates had already established functional transit routines, Al-Hashemi noted that Tehran’s publicized approvals arrived after navigational flows had already stabilized.

The analysis follows recent diplomatic and security discussions held in Baghdad between Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Iraqi officials, during which Tehran agreed to grant exceptional passage permits to designated Iraqi crude tankers navigating the chokepoint.

While state-level agreements sought to address maritime concerns, real-time energy flow tracking indicates that commercial charterers and global energy buyers utilized operational workarounds and alternative navigation protocols to maintain southern crude flows out of Basra’s offshore terminals.

World.title: Iraqi dinar exchange rates hold near 154,500 IQD per $100
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Parallel market exchange rates for the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi Dinar remained elevated across major domestic trading hubs on Tuesday, August 18, 2026, trading at 154,500 IQD per $100 in Baghdad and Basra, and 153,750 IQD in Erbil, according to price sheets published by the 964 Network.

The parallel market pricing maintains a notable spread above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official benchmark rate of 131,000 IQD per $100 (1,310 IQD per $1 USD).

Daily Exchange Rates by City (per $100 USD)

Erbil (Kurdistan Region Main Exchange): Selling Price: 153,750 IQD Buying Price: 153,250 IQD

Basra (Southern Commercial Hub): Selling Price: 154,500 IQD Buying Price: 154,000 IQD



Trading across Baghdad and Basra held steady at a uniform selling level of 154,500 IQD, while Erbil posted a slightly narrower margin at 153,750 IQD per $100.

The persistent parallel market spread reflects ongoing liquidity demand for physical cash dollars in local retail commerce and informal merchant transactions, while institutional cross-border wire transfers and formal import financing continue clearing through the Central Bank’s electronic compliance portal at the official rate.

World.title: 17th Agricultural Week opens in Baghdad: 30M date palm plan and tech deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The 17th Agricultural Week Exhibition for agricultural mechanization, animal production, and food processing officially launched at the Baghdad International Fairgrounds on Saturday, August 22, 2026.

Operating under the theme “Supporting Agriculture to Harvest a Sustainable Future,” the exhibition hosts public- and private-sector pavilions featuring 209 local and international agricultural enterprises showcasing modern farming technology, climate-resilient crop inputs, and livestock pharmaceuticals.

Key Regional Partnerships & Technological Initiatives

1. Saudi-Iraqi Plant Biotechnology & Date Palm Expansion

30 Million Palm Target: Plant tissue culture specialist Saleh Al-Tuwaijri announced a strategic initiative to expand Iraq’s date palm population from approximately 20 million to 30 million trees.

Five-Year Production Capacity: Advanced tissue culture propagation techniques are projected to fulfill 30% to 40% of Iraq’s total seedling requirements over the next five years.

Domestic Biotechnology Labs: With logistical coordination from the Iraqi Ministries of Agriculture and Trade, the Saudi firm finalized the establishment of a specialized plant tissue culture laboratory inside Iraq.

Executive Backing: Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi, accompanied by the Ministers of Agriculture and Trade, toured the biotechnology pavilion during the exhibition to inspect progress and confirm state support.

2. Climate-Resilient Agricultural Solutions (Debbane – Lebanon)

Field Support & Climate Adaptation: Bassem Mohammed Hassan Al-Amin, Director General of Lebanon’s Debbane Modern Agriculture, highlighted that ongoing climate change necessitates specialized heat- and drought-tolerant seeds and soil fertilizers.

Agronomic Field Consulting: Engineering teams are deployed across Iraqi farmlands to deliver on-site technical guidance to optimize seasonal crop yields.

3. Livestock & Veterinary Pharmaceuticals (Syria)

Aviation & Cattle Sector Growth: Ammar Mohammed Al-Qazwini, Director General of the Arab Company for Veterinary Medicine Industries (Syria), noted Iraq’s expanding poultry operations, commercial dairy farms, and feed manufacturing infrastructure.

Cross-Border Veterinary Expertise: Syrian pharmaceutical manufacturers are providing advanced veterinary medicines and poultry treatments to boost local livestock productivity.

The 17th Agricultural Week serves as a regional conduit for introducing climate-adaptive biotechnology, localized seed breeding, and livestock healthcare into Iraq’s domestic farming ecosystem.

By facilitating cross-border investments and establishing domestic biotechnology laboratories, Iraq seeks to strengthen its national date palm reserves, reduce agricultural import dependency, and enhance long-term food security amid ongoing regional climate challenges.

World.title: Iraqi, Saudi ministers discuss energy security, economic integration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair and Finance Minister Faleh al-Sari met with Saudi Energy Minister Abdulaziz bin Salman and Finance Minister Mohammed al-Jadaan in Riyadh on Friday to discuss energy security and economic integration.

The two sides discussed prospects of joint cooperation in the electricity, energy, and gas sectors to achieve the common interests of both Iraq and Saudi Arabia, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Oil Ministry.

The high-level discussions focused on increasing bilateral commerce, stabilizing regional oil supply, and developing an integrated energy infrastructure.

As Iraq plans to increase its oil output from four million barrels per day to between 8 and 10 million barrels per day over the next few years, the Iraqi delegation sought Saudi Arabia’s support to modify its OPEC output share.

The ministers agreed on the next measures to boost cross-border cooperation in the gas, electricity, and power distribution sectors, as well as to improve Iraq’s domestic grid efficiency.

The Iraqi officials indicated that the government is adopting a strategy to reduce dependency on the Strait of Hormuz. The country’s plans include increasing flows through Turkey’s Ceyhan port and exploring alternate transportation routes via Jordan’s Aqaba and Syria’s Baniyas.

The two sides discussed regional security developments, underscoring their shared commitment to sustaining global energy market stability and supply resilience.

World.title: Telecom Minister denies direct starlink deal, confirms EarthLink role
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Jabbar Sanad clarified on Saturday, August 22, 2026, that the Ministry has not signed a direct operational contract with U.S. satellite internet provider Starlink, affirming that domestic telecommunications provider EarthLink remains the state’s primary operational partner under existing service frameworks.

Speaking during a panel session at the 8th Baghdad Dialogue Conference, organized by the Iraqi Institute for Dialogue, Sanad stated that the Ministry seeks to harness market competition to upgrade the country’s digital infrastructure. He noted that while EarthLink and other entities currently provide connectivity, Starlink is slated to transition into a direct partnership role within two years.

Regulatory Oversight and Security Compliance

Participating in the same session, Baligh Abu Kalal, Head of the Communications and Media Commission (CMC), detailed the regulatory and security framework governing satellite internet deployment in Iraq:

Unregulated Terminals: An estimated 40,000 unauthorized Starlink devices were active across Iraq prior to formal regulatory engagement.

National Security Annex: Iraq established a comprehensive security regulatory appendix, making Starlink the first international satellite provider to formally subject its technical operations to Iraqi legal jurisdiction and national security specifications.

Global Precedent: Abu Kalal highlighted that Starlink services operate legally across more than 160 countries worldwide under comparable regulatory frameworks.

Formal Licensing Background: The clarification follows the CMC’s July announcement in the United States—held at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce—confirming the finalization of Starlink’s regulatory license to operate legally within the Iraqi market.

The regulatory track for Starlink reflects Baghdad’s strategy to expand advanced satellite broadband into remote, underserved, and enterprise sectors without undermining existing fiber-optic investments or state regulatory oversight.

By integrating direct licensing with legal compliance protocols, Iraqi authorities aim to regularize existing gray-market hardware, enforce data sovereignty standards, and foster competition across the telecommunications landscape.

World.title: Iran grants exceptional passage for Iraqi oil tankers via Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Following repeated formal requests submitted by the Iraqi government through multiple diplomatic and security channels, Tehran has granted exceptional transit permits for several Iraqi oil tankers, allowing them to navigate through the Strait of Hormuz amid severe maritime insecurity caused by ongoing regional conflict.

According to a report published on Saturday, August 22, 2026, by Iran’s official state news agency, IRNA, securing safe maritime passage for Iraqi crude shipments formed a core agenda item during the recent high-level visit of Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf to Baghdad.

Key Developments & Maritime Details

Exceptional Passage Clearances: Iranian maritime and military authorities approved special security permits facilitating the safe navigation of designated Iraqi crude oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.

Persistent Diplomatic Requests: Baghdad engaged Tehran repeatedly across bilateral channels to secure formal guarantees for Iraqi energy exports traversing the vital chokepoint.

Severe Maritime Friction: Clearances were authorized despite heightened military alerts, stringent navigational restrictions, and active security threats surrounding the strategic waterway.

Bilateral Coordination: The agreement follows strategic talks in Baghdad between Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and senior Iraqi executive and security officials regarding regional stability, border coordination, and energy security.

The Strait of Hormuz remains the single most critical export conduit for southern Iraqi crude originating from the offshore terminals of Basra.

With regional maritime hostilities threatening international shipping lanes and driving up maritime insurance premiums, securing coordinated transit permits helps Baghdad maintain baseline crude export volumes and fulfill international supply commitments while pipeline diversification initiatives remain underway.

World.title: 'We are transforming religious sites across Uttarakhand': CM Dhami in Haridwar
World.content:
HARIDWAR: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami said that "magnificent and divine" Kedarnath has been rebuilt under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi following the 2013 disaster that wreaked havoc.

He said that the state government was focused on transforming religious sites, whether they are in the Kedarkhand region or the Manaskhand region

Addressing the gathering in a programme organised on the occasion of the 51st Nirvana Diwas at Bandichhod here, Dhami on Saturday highlighted the redevelopment of major pilgrimage centres in Uttarakhand and said the state government is working towards the revival and transformation of religious sites through various initiatives.

"Right here in our state, consider Badrinath Dham and Kedarnath Dham; the entire premises there had been devastated and severely damaged following the 2013 disaster," Dhami said.

"Under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, a magnificent and divine Kedarnath has been rebuilt. Inspired and guided by the Prime Minister, we are transforming religious sites across Uttarakhand, whether they are in the Kedarkhand region or the Manaskhand region, into new, revitalised forms through initiatives like the 'Mandir Mala Mission,' undertaking their reconstruction and renewal," he added.

World.title: Ex-diplomat Navdeep Suri flags 'trouble establishing citizenship' during Punjab SIR
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former diplomat

on Sunday said he was facing "trouble establishing his citizenship" during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Punjab, despite having represented India in three countries.

In a post on X, Suri shared his experience with the voter roll revision and said he was asked to provide "unspecified documents" to establish that he was an Indian citizen.

"Sharing my experience with #SIR in Punjab. Went to BLO, submitted Voter ID and Aadhaar card, was assured that everything is in order. Got a message today from a volunteer saying some details donât match with SIR in 2003!" Suri said.

He said that after speaking to the booth-level officer (BLO), he was asked to collect a notice and return with documents proving his citizenship.

"Spoke with BLO, was told that I should come and collect the notice. And then come again with unspecified documents that show I am an Indian citizen. Replied that I was not in India in 2003, so theyâve asked for passport as proof," he added.

Suri said he had documents apart from his voter ID and Aadhaar, but questioned what the process would mean for ordinary citizens.

"I happen to have documents other than voter ID and Aadhaar card.





But canât help asking: If I have trouble establishing my citizenship after representing India in three countries, whatâs the fate of the common citizen? Ease of Living, I presume!" he said.

Former ambassador Navdeep Suri has served as India's high commissioner to Australia and ambassador to UAE and Egypt.

The SIR was first launched in Bihar in June 2025. Following the exercise, more than 60 lakh names, including those of deceased voters, were removed from the electoral rolls.

In West Bengal, around 90 lakh voters were deleted from the rolls ahead of the assembly elections.

Under the SIR process, voters who were not included in the 2002 or 2003 electoral rolls are required to submit documents linking them to people included in those legacy rolls. The Election Commission of India (ECI) had initially listed 11 acceptable documents, excluding Aadhaar.

World.title: ‘Vishwasghaat’: CJP to review Centre’s promises, hints at fresh nationwide protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will convene a meeting of its national working committee on Monday to review the Centreâs commitments that led to the withdrawal of its nationwide agitation on July 25, with the outfit saying that any attempt to backtrack could amount to âvishwasghaatâ (betrayal) with the countryâs youth.

The CJP said the government was yet to formally communicate the steps being taken to fulfil assurances made during talks with the protesters. It said the committee would consider all options to secure implementation of the commitments, including the possibility of launching another peaceful nationwide agitation.

âThe CJP called off its agitation in good faith because the government gave its word to the young people of this country,â CJP said, adding that it would not allow that âgood faithâ to be mistaken for âweaknessâ.

The CJP has also asked students, young citizens, supporters and volunteers to remain prepared for the outcome of Mondayâs meeting.

The warning comes days after the Supreme Court, on August 18, sought a consolidated list of FIRs registered against students and protesters across the country. According to the CJP, the court asked the Centre three times to provide the list so it could consider exercising its powers under Article 142 to quash the cases.





âDespite the court repeatedly asking for this list, the Union government did not commit to providing it,â the CJP said.

The party said that any attempt to âdilute, delay, reinterpret or dishonourâ the commitments, would be seen as âvishwasghaatâ (betrayal) with the country's youth

The outfit said its co-convener Saurav Das and legal affairs lead Ratna Singh raised concerns after the hearing that the government appeared to be âcheatingâ the younger generation by failing to act on the commitments made when the agitation was withdrawn.

Those assurances included withdrawal or quashing of FIRs linked to the protests, a guarantee that students and peaceful protesters would not face punitive action in future, and compensation for families of NEET-UG candidates who died by suicide after the examination was cancelled in May following paper-leak allegations.

NEW DELHI: BJP president Nitin Nabin on Sunday held a meeting with the party's newly appointed office-bearers to discuss its strategy for the 2027 assembly elections in seven states, including Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat.The meeting at the BJP headquarters was attended by senior party functionaries, state unit presidents and state in-charges, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.According to the sources, the meeting focused on strengthening the party's grassroots outreach and its connect with young voters, particularly in states going to polls next year."It's a crucial meeting to discuss a range of organisational matters with prime focus on the party's preparations and strategy for the upcoming elections in states next year," a source told PTI.Assembly elections are due in Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Goa and Himachal Pradesh in 2027. The BJP is currently in power in four of these states - Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Uttarakhand and Goa. The Aam Aadmi Party governs Punjab, while the Congress is in power in Himachal Pradesh.Earlier on Saturday, Nabin held his first interaction with the newly appointed office-bearers as well as members of the previous BJP national team.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also visited the BJP headquarters on Saturday and interacted with all 67 newly appointed national office-bearers. His meeting with the party leaders lasted more than five hours."Organisational meetings are all about new ideas and perspectives aimed at strengthening the Party and deepening connect with the people. Great interaction with fellow party colleagues and the new organisational team," Modi said in a post on social media, sharing pictures from the meeting.According to PTI, Modi listened to each office-bearer and offered suggestions, urging the new team to expand its outreach, connect with young people and increase its grassroots presence.BJP national office-bearers' meeting on Saturday also passed a resolution criticising the Congress over its decision to sing only two stanzas of Vande Mataram at its events.The party vowed to protect the "dignity and the national status" of the full version of the national song and announced a nationwide campaign to highlight its significance.In a 10-point resolution, the BJP said it would educate and mobilise people, particularly the younger generation, about all six stanzas of Vande Mataram and its history.The party also said a resolution of the Congress Working Committee cannot override constitutional institutions or laws enacted by Parliament."A political compromise of 1937 cannot be elevated above the constitutional settlement of 1950 and legislation enacted by Parliament in 2026," the BJP said in its resolution.

World.title: Sajjan Kumar ‘role model’ row: Haryana Cong leader urges Kharge to remove Hooda from CWC
World.content:
Senior Haryana Congress leader

on Sunday urged party president Mallikarjun Kharge to remove Rohtak MP

from the Congress Working Committee (CWC). Sharma accused Hooda of praising former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, whose death has reignited a political row over the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.

Sharma, a former speaker of the Haryana Assembly, accused Hooda of âextolling the virtuesâ of Kumar as a role model, saying the remarks had caused resentment within the Sikh community and could hurt the Congress ahead of the Punjab polls.

âEver since Deepender Hooda, a permanent invitee to the CWC, issued a statement extolling the virtues of Sajjan Kumar, since deceased, as a role model, it has sent shock waves among the Sikh community,â Sharma said in his letter to Kharge, PTI reported.

âA few of my Sikh friends from Haryana and Punjab called me to express their resentment over such an irresponsible statement,â he added.

Sharma said the remarks could affect the Congress' support among Sikh voters.

âSuch a statement by Deepender Hooda on the eve of

has not only harmed the partyâs interests, but has opened the wounds of the Sikh community all over again. It is needless to say that the Congress had disassociated itself from Sajjan Kumar completely,â he wrote.





He urged Kharge to remove Hooda from the CWC, saying his âimmature and irresponsible remarks have weakened the Congress, especially in the eyes of the Sikh communityâ.

Hooda, however, denied using the words ârole modelâ or expressing such a sentiment. Speaking to reporters in Gurugram on Sunday, he said, âI did not use the words, nor did I harbour any such sentiment. These words are being put in my mouth by those who wish to play politics by undermining the spirit of brotherhood.â

âAs for the Sikh community, people know that we have always stood by them and supported them in every way,â he added.

Meanwhile, Punjab Congress leaders have also distanced themselves from Hooda's remarks. Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said the statement reflected Hooda's personal view.

âWhat Rohtak MP Deepender Hooda said, that may be his personal view,â Warring told reporters, while stressing that the 1984 riots remained a painful chapter.

âDespite the passage of so much time, the trauma runs deep in people's minds. As for Deepender Hooda said, that may be his personal view,â he said.

Former Punjab chief minister and Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi was more direct in his criticism, saying Kumar âshould have been shot publiclyâ for his role in the riots.

World.title: Piyush Goyal heads for Japan with business delegation to boost trade, investments
World.content:
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal is leading a 200-member business delegation to Japan on a four-day visit starting August 24 to boost trade and investment ties between the two countries.

The visit assumes significance since Japan set an investment target last year of 10 trillion yen in (about ₹60,000 crore) India over a decade.

The Minister will travel to Tokyo, Nagoya, and Osaka.

The business delegation has representatives from various sectors, ranging from manufacturing, semiconductors, clean energy, steel, automotive, financial services, healthcare to start-ups, industry chamber Ficci Director General Jyoti Vij told reporters in Tokyo.

In Tokyo, Mr. Goyal will hold a series of meetings with the top leadership of major Japanese conglomerates and industrial houses that have long been partners in India's growth, alongside a round-table with the Keidanren (Japan Business Federation), representing over 1,500 leading Japanese companies.

Dedicated sessions are planned on semiconductors, artificial intelligence, start-ups, and engagement with foreign institutional investors, reflecting India's growing pull as an investment and innovation destination.

Bilateral talks

The Minister will also hold bilateral talks with his counterpart, Akazawa Ryosei, Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry, and call on senior members of the Japanese Government and Parliament, besides interacting with the Indian community in Japan.

Similarly in Nagoya, the industrial heartland of Central Japan, the Minister will lead a roadshow with Chukeiren (Central Japan Economic Federation), and the Nagoya Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and engage with the Aichi Prefecture leadership and major manufacturing investors in the automotive and steel sectors.

The visit will conclude in Osaka with an investors and business roadshow, along with meetings with leading Japanese companies across electronics, industrial, and consumer sectors, aimed at showcasing opportunities across India's manufacturing, clean energy and consumer markets.

The visit is expected to give fresh momentum to bilateral trade and investment ties, and open new avenues of cooperation in high-technology manufacturing and next-generation industries, the Commerce Ministry said in a statement.

Ms. Vij said discussions with Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO), Japanese business organisations and investors will focus on opportunities for Japanese companies in India and ways to facilitate greater two-way investment.

"The programme includes engagements with organisations and companies working in digital innovation, industrial transformation, advanced manufacturing, AI, semiconductors and electronics," she said, adding that deliberations will include increasing cooperation in capital goods, machinery, automotive and advanced manufacturing.

The delegation will highlight India's growing opportunities in manufacturing, technology, electronics, automotive, start-ups and other high-growth sectors, while encouraging Japanese companies to expand their presence and investments in India.

Trade pact

The two countries are looking at reviewing the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which came into effect on August 1, 2011. The seventh Joint Committee Meeting under the India-Japan CEPA was held on March 2 this year in Tokyo.

India has emphasised the need for a more balanced bilateral trade relationship to ensure long-term sustainability. The country has called for the review of the pact as the trade deficit is increasing.

The review assumes significance as domestic steel producers have complained of a surge in imports of steel products like hot-rolled steel and other variants from Japan.

On the other hand, Japanese firms have earlier flagged issues with regard to Indian quality control orders.

FDI from Japan

Japan is the fifth largest investor in India. India received $48.14 billion in FDI between April 2000 and March 2026. Japan accounted for 6% of total FDI attracted by India during the period.

The two-way commerce between the countries grew 9.18 per cent to $27.47 billion (exports of $6.03 billion and imports of $21.43 billion) in 2025-26 from $25.16 billion in 2024-25.

The trade deficit between the countries increased to $15.4 billion in the last fiscal year from $12.66 billion in 2024-25.

World.title: Three MPs accuse NDA of trying to retain power through delimitation and oppose FCRA Bill
World.content:
Three Members of Parliament of the Congress, the CPI and the MDMK expressed their strong opposition to any proposed delimitation and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill (FCRA), 2026, in its present form.

At a symposium organised here on Sunday, they said the delimitation was specially targeted against the southern States which had shown measures in controlling population rise while the FCRA Bill would adversely affect even the poorer sections besides the minorities and the organisations run by them once it becomes an Act, the MPs felt.

Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Minister Ramesh, who participated, categorically said the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay would not remain a spectator when difficulties arose for the minorities. The government was also “firm” in its stand to freeze the number of Lok Sabha seats at the existing 543.

Highlighting some of the controversial clauses in the FCRA Bill, Tiruchi MP Durai Vaiko (MDMK) said minority educational institutions were playing a pivotal role in the field of education and services because of which Tamil Nadu was in the forefront today. The FCRA Bill would not only affect the minorities who run several educational institutions and hospitals but also hit the poorer sections getting benefited by it not only in Tamil Nadu but all over the country, he said. It was because of the stiff resistance from the Opposition in Parliament that the contentious FCRA Bill had been referred to the Joint Parliamentary Committee, he said. Mr. Durai Vaiko charged the BJP-led NDA government with trying to deceive the people on the Delimitation Bill and stressed the need for opposing it as it would affect the interests of southern States.

Nagapattinam MP V. Selvaraj (CPI) said the NDA was trying to consolidate its position in the northern States and stage a comeback without the support of southern States by proposing delimitation and the FCRA Bill was directed against the minorities and the organisations run by them.

Congress Rajya Sabha member M. Christopher Tilak said India was a nation of many minorities and “a false narrative” was being spread that the foreign contributions were being used for conversion.

Indian Union Muslim League national president K.M. Kader Mohideen said the apprehensions of the minorities on the FCRA Bill in its present form should be conveyed to the Joint Parliamentary Committee members in person in the form of a memorandum. He called upon the MPs from Tamil Nadu to help the minority community in clarifying their position to the Committee on the FCRA Bill.

World.title: No new H1N1 strain in India, existing vaccines sufficient, says ICMR
World.content:
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) on Sunday (August 23, 2026) said that the Influenza A (H1N1) viruses currently circulating in the country belong to the A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1) pdm09-like virus strain. It clarified that no new strain of H1N1 has been identified and there is no cause for panic.

“These viruses belong to clade 6B.1A.5a2a, subclade D.3.1.1, and have been in circulation since 2025. The Influenza strains currently circulating are also well matched with the vaccine strains recommended for the Northern Hemisphere,” ICMR said. “Seasonal influenza, including H1N1, is mostly self-limiting,” it added.

Common symptoms of the illness include fever, cough, headache, and body ache, and most people recover with appropriate care and rest. However, young children, elderly persons, and individuals with underlying medical conditions may be at a greater risk of complications. If symptoms persist, worsen, or become severe, consultation with a doctor is advised, it said.

The Union Health Ministry has said that it is closely monitoring the situation through regular surveillance and is undertaking necessary public health measures.

India has registered a rise in seasonal Influenza A(H1N1) cases, commonly called swine flu, this monsoon, especially in major cities. Delhi has reported 1,777 confirmed H1N1 cases so far this year, including 114 new cases on August 20. Karnataka has registered over 4,000 cases, with more than half reported from Bengaluru. Rising influenza activity has also been reported in Mumbai, Chennai and parts of Kerala.

National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) data show that H1N1 activity was relatively low in 2021 (778 cases, 12 deaths) after the pandemic period, but rebounded sharply in 2022 (13,202 cases, 410 deaths) and remained substantial in 2023 (8,125 cases, 129 deaths). By June 2024, India had already recorded 7,215 cases and 150 deaths, and year-end numbers were higher. NCDC’s 2025 reporting shows that H1N1 continued to circulate across multiple States.

NCDC maintains a nationwide influenza surveillance network and publishes State-wise data and H1N1 treatment/prevention guidelines. It recommends seasonal influenza vaccination based on WHO strain recommendations. For the 2025–26 season, India’s recommended trivalent vaccine included H1N1, H3N2 and B/Victoria components, with circulating Indian H1N1 strains aligning with vaccine strains.

“People at higher risk should consider annual vaccination and seek medical advice promptly if flu symptoms become severe,” Anil Bansal of the Delhi Medical Association said.

World.title: Five held for kidnapping, assaulting dry fruit traders in Begum Bazar
World.content:
Goshamahal police have arrested five persons for allegedly confining and assaulting two dry fruit traders and demanding ₹2 lakh and the surrender of a car and an auto for their release in Begum Bazar.

The arrested persons were identified as Karan Kumar, Hanuman Ram, Devi Lal, Shambhu Kumar and Jumar alias Jumar Gujjar. Police said six other accused persons, including Shubham Parihar, Tharun, Manish, Praveen, Pankaj and Datta, were absconding and efforts were on to apprehend them.

According to the police, the complainant, Mohd Akbar, and his brother Mohd Aleem had been procuring dry fruits from Vinod Impex in Begum Bazar for about two years. Police said the two were accused of financial irregularities involving about ₹8 lakh, allegedly by forging the firm’s stamp, over the past three months.

On August 20, Karan Kumar, the owner of Vinod Impex, and his associates allegedly confined the brothers inside a godown, assaulted them with their hands and steel pipes, tied their hands and threatened to circulate videos of them on social media, police said.

Their parents were also allegedly called to the godown, confined and abused, according to the complaint. The accused allegedly demanded ₹2 lakh and the surrender of one car and one auto for releasing them. The alleged confinement and assault continued until the early hours of August 21.

The parties were subsequently taken to Goshamahal police station, where Akbar and Aleem reportedly informed the police about the assault and confinement. They were sent to Osmania General Hospital for medical examination and treatment in view of their injuries.

Police registered a case under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to kidnapping for ransom, hurt, criminal intimidation and other offences.

On August 22, police received information that Karan Kumar and Hanuman Ram were at the former’s residence, while Devi Lal, Shambhu Kumar and Jumar were near the Fish Market in Begum Bazar. Police teams reached the locations and apprehended the five men.

The accused were arrested and produced before the XVI ACJM court before being remanded, police said. A Swift Dzire, an Indica car, an auto and two mobile phones were seized during the investigation.

Police said efforts were under way to apprehend the remaining accused.

World.title: KPSC ‘scam’ case: ED raids IAS officer Gangwar's premises in Karnataka, U.P.
World.content:
A day after IAS officer and MSME Director Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar returned from his hometown in Uttar Pradesh after being out of contact for nearly two days, Directorate of Enforcement (ED) officials, on Sunday (August 23, 2026), reportedly arrived at his residential premises in Bengaluru in connection with the ongoing probe into alleged irregularities in KPSC recruitment.

Mr. Gangwar had served as the Controller of Examinations at the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) when the veterinary officer recruitment examination was conducted. The recruitment process has come under the ED's scanner following allegations of large-scale irregularities and claims that candidates were asked to pay huge sums of money.

The ED had earlier conducted searches at several locations in connection with the case, including the residence of former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar and premises linked to veterinary officers. Officials are also investigating allegations that candidates were asked to pay between ₹70 lakh and ₹80 lakh for securing appointments.

On Sunday, an ED team reached Mr. Gangwar’s apartment in Bengaluru in three vehicles, accompanied by CRPF personnel. Security personnel initially locked the apartment gate and told the officials that they were instructed not to allow anyone inside.

The officials reportedly spent nearly two hours at the premises, attempting to gain access to the apartment. According to reports, they contacted Mr. Gangwar, after which the security personnel allowed them into the apartment complex.

However, the officials allegedly found the residence locked, and Mr. Gangwar was not present. His phone was said to be switched off.

The ED team subsequently called a locksmith to the premises to prepare a duplicate key to open the apartment. The officials also arranged for a neighbour to be present as a witness while the door was being opened.

The developments come shortly after Mr. Gangwar’s brief absence from Bengaluru sparked speculation amid the ED investigation. Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge said that the IAS officer had travelled to Uttar Pradesh to meet his ailing father and that his absence was linked to a family emergency.

While Mr. Gangwar’s role as Controller of Examinations has brought him under the ED’s scrutiny, there is no confirmed information establishing that he himself has been accused of accepting bribes or participating in the alleged recruitment scam. The allegations remain part of the ongoing investigation, sources said.
